lawyer:
Md Khalilur Rahman, Advocate—For the Plaintiffs-Appellants. 

Sashanka Shekhor Sarkar, Deputy Attorney-General—For the Defendants-Respondents.
parties:
Abul Kalam alias Kaliullah and others ------ Plaintiffs-Appellants
Vs.
Madhab Bigraho and others ------ Defendants-Respondents
full_judgment:
3. The case of plaintiffs is that, suit land originally belongs to Bhawal Raj. The suit land of schedule 'Ka' comprising of an area of 23.13 acres of land recorded in CS khatian No. 7 along with other lands in the name of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Chowdhury settled the suit land in raiyati right. On the death of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, his heirs as of tenanted right was owner in possession of the entire land of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. As per Court of Wards Act 1879, the management and administration of the property including "Ka" schedule land of CS khatian No.  7 was taken over by the Court of Wards. During the last CS record, it was recorded in the name of Court of Wards, for Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and others, which was subsequently named as Bhawal Raj Courts of Wards Estate or Bhawal Court of Wards Estate or Court of Wards Bhawal Raj Estate. Bhawal Court of Wards Estate as owner and possessor of `Ka' schedule land with other lands of CS khatian No.  7, settled 'Ka' schedule land with the father and husband of the plaintiff. Bashoruddin and co-sharer, Chand Mia through its own printed pattannama. Basiruddin and Chand Mia became owner and possessor in equal share. While Basiruddin and Chand Mia on the basis of pattannama and dakhila and by paying zamindari taxes to Bhawal Court of Wards Estate, the Government, then province of East Pakistan by giving effect of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act acquired the rent receiving interest of the Zaminder and on taking nominal taxes as land development tax, the tenants were classified as owner of their respective land as per sections 3 and 42 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. After acquisition of the rent receiving interest as aforesaid, Government published final gazette as per provision of section 3 of the aforesaid Act on 24-3-1952. After acquisition of the land as aforesaid, Compensation Assessment Roll were prepared and Zaminder as per the aforesaid compensation assessment roll received compensation and gazette was published on 29-5-1956 as per section 42 of the aforesaid Act by which the Zamindari of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury of `Ka' schedule land, was acquired and the status of tenant. Basiruddin and Chand Mia were changed and become owners. Accordingly SA khatian was finally published in their names. By opening jote in the revenue office and by paying nominal land development tax possessing the suit land SA khatian No.  63 was finally published in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia in equal 8 annas share. Basiruddin and Chand Mia upon an amicable settlement partitioned the kha schedule land by which 'Ka' schedule land fallen in the saham of Basiruddin. After acquisition of the land by the Government, 5.40 acres of land remain in the hand of Basiruddin alone which has been mentioned in 'Kha' schedule. Chand Mia got 'Ga' schedule land which comprising of 0.39 acres of land of dag No. 155/1061, 0.51 acres of land of dag No. 1059, 1.42 acres of land of dag No. 1063, 1.18 acres of land of dag No. 1058, 0.60 acres of land of dag No. 1060, in total, 4.10 acres of land and remaining land, in total 13.36 acres including 12.5 as mentioned in 'Gha' schedule was in ejmlali and co-sharers as owners owned and possessed by cultivation. While the aforesaid land was in possession of co-sharers, 1.48 acres of land was acquired by the Government out of 13.63 acres of land for road and remaining land i.e. 12.15 acres of land, "Gha' schedule, was in ejmali of the co-sharers. While co-sharers as aforesaid was in possession having title there to, Government acquired portion of land for defendant No. 16, the Ministry of Agriculture, defendant No. 17, Rice Research Institution from the land of Chand Mia to the very knowledge of defendant No.  1 and 14 in LA Case No.  100/65-66, recognizing Chand Mia as the owner of the aforesaid land. Compensation was received by Chand Mia while in possession, 12.15 acres of land described in schedule `Gha', constructed homestead, planted trees and cultivated agricultural lands in ejmali, died leaving, defendant No.  6 as heir who along with other co-sharers possessing the land in ejmali. While defendant No. 6, plaintiff and Chand Mia was in possession of the ejmali property of 'Gha' schedule comprising 12.15 acres, Government in LA case No.  5/85-86 acquired 10 acres of land for defendant No.  19, Gazipur District Police Line under defendant No.  18, Ministry of Home Affairs. In LA Case No.  3/2001-2002 Government acquired 0.33 acres of land for defendant No.  26, District Fisheries Officer under defendant No.  25, Ministry of Fisheries and Veterinaries under Government of Bangladesh, in LA Case No.  7/90-91 acquired 0.09 acres of land for defendant No. 20, District Jail, Gazipur under defendant No.  18, Ministry of Home Affairs, in LA Case No.  3/95-96 acquired 0.33 acres of land for Defendant No.  District primary Education office under defendant No. 21 Ministry of Education, Government of Bangladesh, in LA Case No.  5/90-91 acquired .50 acres of land for defendant No.  24, Public Health Engineering Department under defendant No.  23, Ministry of Health, Government of Bangladesh. Government disbursed compensation money part of the afore-said 5 LA cases to the plaintiffs and to the co-sharers having found they are legal title holder. Some greedy person of the locality created obstruction in getting compensation money and gave proposal to defendant No. 6, son of defendant No. 9 and brother of defendant Nos.  1 and 8, but recognized their title over 'Kha' schedule land when they would manage in getting the compensation money to the plaintiffs. Later on, Chand Mia died leaving defendant Nos.  2-5 as heirs. Plaintiffs, the heirs of Chand Mia, defendant Nos. 2-5 are waiting for getting compensation money. Suddenly, on 12-12-2007 the manager of defendant No. 14 and the officer of Bhawal Court of Wards came to 'Kha' schedule land whereupon plaintiff could know that defendant No. 1 of the instant suit along with defendant No. 1 of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 filed in the court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur against defendant Nos. 3-6, in total against 11 persons as defendants and they got decree. Defendant No. 1 of the instant suit got decree up to the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. In RS record 18.70 acres of land of 'Kha' schedule recorded in the name of defendant No. 1 and they requested plaintiffs to give up possession of the suit land. Defendant No.  1 of the instant suit threatened plaintiff that if they did not give up possession to the defendant No.  14 amicably then they by force evicted the plaintiffs from the suit land. Plaintiffs went to defendant No.  14 to know about the decree, then, the manager of defendant No.  14, Abdur Rouf, gave a paper book to plaintiff No.  1 and requested plaintiff No.  1 to go through paper book to find out how the suit was decreed. Plaintiffs after getting paper book asked defendant Nos.  6 and 3 as to how they got decree in the suit to which they kept silence. Defendant No. 1 with connivance with defendant Nos.  6-13 got the decree surreptitiously. 

 4. It is further case of plaintiffs that defendant No. 1 was never owner and possessor of the suit land from defendant No.  14 in any manner either as tenant or as Raiyat. The lands upon which defendant No. 1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho claimed title Extinguished from the moment State Acquisition of Tenancy Act published in gazette on 24-3-1952 and vested in the Government, as such, defendant No. 1 looses his right to collect rent from the plaintiffs or any-body. 

 5. It is further case of plaintiffs that, defendant Nos.  1 to 14 in connivance with the employees of Deputy Commissioner turned the relevant portions of SA khatian which was kept in the record room of Deputy Commissioner but the said SA khatian having been kept in other offices like tahsil, AC Land office including DG, DLR office of the Government wherein the said SA khatian with index is found and on scrutinizing of SA khatian No.  63 it appears that said SA khatian No.  63 was prepared in the name of predecessor of Basiruddin and Chand Mia and on the basis of said SA record the other document i.e. for collection of the rent, i.e. talab baki register which is retisger-2 and from Union land office, earlier Tohsil Office it is seen the record stand, in the name of plaintiffs predecessor and in index in different LA Cases, wherein on the basis of said SA khatian No.  63, lands were acquired and compensation money were disbursed in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia. It is seen that the aforesaid khatian was prepared in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia. 

 6. It is further case of plaintiffs that during final survey prior to RS record, recorded the name of plaintiffs but employees of survey settlement department recorded otherwise in finally published RS khatian. On the basis of the aforesaid SA khatian No. 63, Government acquired land for defendant No.  17, Bangladesh Rice Research Institute and also for other Government machineries. The aforesaid RS khatian No. 506 was prepared wrongly in the name of defendant No. 1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho in the name of Shebayet of Deity Sarju Bala in 8 annas share and in the name of Bivabati Devi, wife of, Kumar Ramcendra Narayan Ray Chowdhury in 8 annas share whose name had not been recorded in CS as well as SA khatian. 

 10. The case of defendant Nos.  1 and 14 is that, suit land was recorded in CS khatian Nos.  7 and 770 ultimately in RS khatian No.  506 and 1011 and quantum of land was 23.13. Original owner of the suit property was Kumar Rabindra Narayant Roy Chowdhury and others and later, Bhawal Court of Wards. While Chowdhuries were in possession, they installed family deity as Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho and puja expenses were paid from their own income. The aforesaid Bhawal Raj for maintaining the deity for worship, handed over their entire property to Bhawal Court of Wards under Court of Wards Act, 1879 and from 1911 Court of Wards maintained the case property on behalf of Bhawal Raj Estate. CS record recorded the name of Court of Wards on behalf of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and other co-sharers. Bhawal Raj maintained the Estate by giving barga and adi Barga, maintained possession, Vz portion of the crops was given to the manager and remaining 1A portion to the cultivator. Manager as shebayet, by the income worshiping the family deity. The name of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho is correctly recorded in RS khatian. Suits were filed for and against Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho and decree was passed in favour of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho. The case of plaintiffs is false. 

 12. The case of defendant Nos.  16 to 32 is that Gha schedule of the suit land has been acquired by the Government in LA Case No. 100/65-66, LA Case Nos.  5/85-86, 5/90-91, 3/ 95-96, 3/2001-2002 and 7/90-91 giving compensation money to the plaintiffs and his co-sharers. In SA khatian No. 63,23.13 decimals of land recorded in the name of Basiruddin in 8 annas share. In RS khatian No.  506,18/3 acres of land has been recorded in the name of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho in 8 annas share. The Government has no claim excepting the land which has been acquired by the Government where Government has title. 

 17. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiff appellants, submits that, pattannama exhibit-2 was disbelieved by the learned Judge on the ground that dates mentioned therein in Bengali has no similarity with the corresponding English date without properly going through the contents thereof as the date in Bengali mentioned in the middle side of the pattannama is the preliminary date of pattan subject to the approval of the Chief Manager and the date in English after signature of the concerned Nayeb of Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate is the date after approval of the pattan by the Chief Manager of the said Court of Wards. Learned Advocate further submits that judgment passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 and also of those of the higher Courts up to the Appellate Division wherein decision arrived are not supported by law as the lands of SA Khaian No.  63 of the suit land was settled as pr6jabili and as per President Order No. 90 of 1972 no suit can be filed against the lands settled as projabili as such said judgment having passed on wrong assumption of law affirmed up to Appellate Division is a judgment per in curium. Learned Advocate submits that rent receipts were granted by the Zaminder and thereafter, by the Revenue Authority of the Government after whole sale acquisition of the land and on the face of such legal position, preparation of RS khatian in the name of defendant No. 1 is without any basis, the court below without considering the materials on record abruptly hold pattanana as forged which finding is erroneous in as much as the names of Basiruddin and Chand Mia was duly recorded in the subsequent documents like Register II, the Talab Baki Register, exhibit-5, Compensation Assessment Roll, exhibit-8, rent receiver's Title Description Register, exhibit-4 and lastly in SA khatian, record of right after effecting the 'projapattani'. Learned Advocate further submits that document filed connecting with projapattani being more than 30 years old and has been produced from proper custody of the plaintiff-appellants got presumptive value of its execution and further submits that learned Judge committed gross illegality in holding that SA khatian produced form, the side of plaintiffs is a created document upon using a revenue stamp and bears no signature of Officer-in-Charge of record room is baseless and against the record and also against order No.  68 dated 30-11-2009 passed by the learned Judge on the application filed by the plaintiffs for calling the record from the Revenue Department whereupon the court ordered that since Government produced SA khatian as such record from Revenue Department is not required to be called to settle the dispute without considering that Government produced distorted SA khatian. Learned Advocate further submits that the findings of the learned Judge that in Title Suit No. 12 of 1976 it is decided Chand Mia is a bargadar under defendant No. 1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho is baseless and fully on surmise and conjecture as the contesting defendant-respondent No. 1 and 14 who claimed their title through those judgments, had neither filed nor exhibited those judgment in the present suit as such finding of the learned Judge that Chand Mia had admitted in those previous suits that he was a bargadar is baseless and full of surmise and conjecture not supported by any law. Learned Advocate further submits that court below was in erroneous findings of fact as it should have considered the vital documents like the rent receiving interest acquisition gazettes, exhibit Nos. 7 and 9, written statements of defendant Nos.  6 to 32, true copy of the SA khatian produced by the Government, exhibit No.  `Kha; the register No. II i.e. Talab Baki Register, exhibit No. 5, Compensation Assessment Roll exhibit No. 8 and the rent receiver's Title Description Register, exhibit No. 4, which are although in certified copies are not challenged by the Government while marked as exhibits and non-consideration of those vital documents led the Court below to erroneous finding as to the title of the plaintiffs-appellants. Learned Advocate further submits that possession of the plaintiffs-appellants from the time of pattan upto the date of forceful eviction on 3-3-2008 and 5-3-2008 has been proved by the oral and documentary evidences of the plaintiffs-appellants and also by the defendant's witnesses, DW 1 and DW 2, learned Judge committed gross illegality in not declaring title of the plaintiffs over the suit property by adverse possession. Learned Advocate further submits that possession of the plaintiffs have been proved through municipal tax receipts, electric and gas bills, house rent receipts etc. exhibit 13 series and also Advocate Commissioner's report and such non-consideration of those vital documents as to possession of the plaintiffs led the Court to an erroneous finding as to title of the plaintiffs, as possession follows title. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No.  1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho having not been represented by the Shebayet in the previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 2985 as plaintiff and in the subsequent present Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 as defendant No.  1 and the defendant No.  14 the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate having no connection with the deity, has no locus standi to file the previous Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 and also to contest the subsequent Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 as its representative, so, the decree passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 and the dismissal decree passed in Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 is illegal and without jurisdiction. Learned Advocate further submits that neither defendant No. 1 nor defendant No.  14 filed any document of acquiring title in the suit property nor proved their possession therein, but the learned trial court dismissed the suit on coming to the conclusion on surmise that the defendant No. 1 is a owner of the suit property. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 14 having admitted that all the properties except ‘Kha' schedule property have been acquired by the Government and also compensation have been paid to the plaintiffs and Chand Mia, decree passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 for recovery of khas possession of the entire 18.73 acres of land including the acquired land, is illegal and not binding upon the persons in possession through acquisition. 

 21. The aforesaid points taken up for consideration may be summarized as to whether i) the 'Kha' schedule 5.40 acre suit property and other 18.73 acre property total 23.13 acre property recorded in the admitted CS khatian No.  7 was a projabili property under the jamindar, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Ray Chowdhury represented by Court of Wards and as to whether ii) the plaintiffs appellants' predecessor, Bosar Uddin and his co-sharer Chand Miah were projas under the said judgment or that the defendant No. 1 Sree Sree Madab Bigraha was the proja under the said jamindar and lasty as to whether iii) the lower court below is correct in dismissing the suit by impugned judgment. 

 26. When people of Bengal particularly muslims were oppressed like animals at the hand of such Zaminders, Sher-e-Bangla AK Fazlul Huq stood against this system. In the book of Osamapta Atma Kahini Sheikh Mujibur Rahman written it was one of the point for Pakistan movement to abolish Zamindari system. Mr Huq took this point as in his early days he saw a little boy was playing with a 'Kasha' plate when Mr Huq was passing the boy but while returning, he saw the little boy crying as men of Zaminders snatched the plate for nonpayment of taxes from the little boy. Mr Huq took it a point that if he could attain such a position to dictate the terms he will abolish this hated system. It was finally abolish given the tenants maliki when Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was in power through PO 90 of 1972. 

 42. Plaintiffs case is that they got pattern of the land from Zaminder of Bhawal and since then they are in possession, at first, under the Zaminder and later on, under the Government until dispossess in 2008. The case of defendant Nos.  1 and 2 is that property having belongs to a deity, this property could not be alienated by anyone except legal necessity; RS khatian prepared rightly, plaintiffs title has been extinguished and defendant No. 1 having got decree in Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 this suit was dismissed rightly. The case of defendant No.  6 is that he was not a party to Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 as he did not appeared in the suit and his father's name was not rightly recorded. It is the case of defendant No.  6 that defendant No. 1 had no title nor possession and on the basis of decree of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 defendant Nos.  1 and 14 illegally threatened plaintiffs from dispossession from the suit land. Defendant Nos.  6-17 wants saham for 4.10 acres of land which has been acquired for Bangladesh Rice Research Institute. The case of defendant Nos.  16 to 32 is that the suit land has been acquired from plaintiffs by different LA Cases and suit land has been rightly recorded in the name of plaintiffs and SA, khatian No. 63 in 8 annas equal share to Basiruddin, predecessor of the plaintiffs and Chand Mia, predecessor of the defendant Nos.  2 and 6. 

 43. It appears that Government in written statement admitted plaintiffs are the owner of the suit property as in the written statement Government stated that in different LA Cases Government acquired land from plaintiffs and from their co-sharer and SA Khatian No.  63 was rightly prepared in the name of predecessor of the plaintiffs and also of his co-sharer, Chand Mia and it is also the case of the Government that plaintiff of Title Suit No 1219 of 1985 and defendant No.  1 of the instant suit has no title or possession. As such, title of the plaintiffs has well established. On this background let us refer to the depositions of the witnesses particularly of defendant's witnesses who stated as:— 

 48. This pattannama has been acted upon as from exhibit-3 series it appears that the pat-tan holder paid Zaminderi tax up to 1942 then from exhibit No. 4, dakhila, it appears land has been recorded as 'projabili' extinguishing title of Superior landlord, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. From exhibit No.  2-4 it appears from the column of the khatian that name of plaintiffs and co-sharer have been recorded for 23.13 acres of land as projabili. Exhibt-5 is Talib Baki Register-II kept in the custody of Government where also we find the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs from whom tax was collected. Exhibit-6 series are rent receipts stand in the name of plaintiffs and their predecessor. Up to this plaintiffs have been able to prove that they have paid rent to the Zaminder pursuant to the pattan taken from Zaminder i.e. up to 1952. 

 49. Since Gazette has been published as projabili and thereafter, State Acquisition and Tenancy Act washed away Zamindari system, plaintiff became owner of their respective land as it is asserted by provision of law. 

 50. From Dhaka gazette, published on Monday, March, 1954, it appears that Zaminderi system has been abolished and it was taken over by the Government giving status of tenant of land as 'Malik'. Let us quote from the gazette itself:- which runs as:— 

 51. So, after promulgation of the gazette in 1952, March, 24, Zamindari system having been abolished the plaintiffs predecessor became land owner. Section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act speaks that rents receiving interest has been devolved upon the Government not upon the Zaminder. Exhibit-7, a copy of Dhaka gazette wherein the suit land has been included. Exhibit-8, compensation assessment roll shows that some lands were acquired by the Government from the predecessor of the plaintiffs taking them as 'Malik' of the suit land as projabili. Exhibit-9 also a copy of Dhaka Gazette, the last gazette published under State Acquisition and Tenancy Act includes the suit land as:— 

 "Under the provision of sub-section (2) of section 43 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act No.  XXVIII of 1951), read with section 46 C of the said Act, the Governor is pleased to declare that Compensation Assessment-rolls in respect of such properties of the rent-receivers mentioned in the Schedule below as have been acquire under section 3 or will be deemed to be acquired under clause (3) of section 46 E of that Act, have been finally published under section 42 of the said Act on the date shown against each." 

 52. Exhibit-11 official document, a notice, issued as per section 3 for acquiring the land by the Additional land Acquisition Officer, Gazipur to Chand Mia and also to the predecessor of the plaintiffs. This document goes to show continued possession of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land. In front of all these government documents RS khatian was published in the name of defendant No. 1 showing Surjabala Debi and Bibhabatibala Debi, wife of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury as possessor in 8 annas share each is totally baseless. It is admitted position that RS khatian was prepared in between 1969-1985. 

 54. Bhawal Raj is known to all of Bangladesh for many reasons including the famous case of Mejo Kumar and Bhibaboti Debi. For this reason family of Bhwal Raj is well known to all of us. It is also known that Bhibaboti Bala Debi as well Surjabala Debi left this country (East Bengal) just after pronouncement of judgment in 1919, as such, in 1985 their names cannot appear as possessors in the RS khatian, as such, it can be definitely said that RS khatian has been prepared illegally without any basis. 

 "It is to be further observed that it is now well settled on the authority of Jalil Ahmed vs the Province of East Pakistan: (1967) 19 DLR 106 decided by a Special Bench and affirmed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Tanvir Ahmed Siddiki vs the Province of East Pakistan (1968) 20 DLR (SC) 144 PLD 1968 SC 185 that on the publication of the notification under section 3 of the Act, all rent receiving interests including that of Debuttor and Waqf estate stood acquired and all non-retainable khas land also stood vested in the Government." In paragraph 4 of the judgment, it is held: "There is another fact which needs to be noted that in the year 1963 notifications under section 43 of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been published acquiring of all interests other than already acquired under section 3 of the Act completing all acquisition proceedings under the Act. All the notifications have been published in the Official Gazette covering all districts of Bangladesh. Another fact that requires to be noted is that President's Order No. 90 of 1972, the Bangladesh (Legal Proceedings) (Third) Order 1972, was promulgated on 3rd August, 1972 long after the observation made in some of the decisions of the High Court, Dacca on the retention by the Mutwalli or Shebait of an estate on account of non-preparation of the compensation assessment roll. This enactment has been promulgated long after all the acquisition proceedings were completed and long after the observations of the High Court made regarding the non-preparation of the compensation assessment roll. This enactment made in President' Order No.  90 of 1972 clearly states that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act No.  XXVIII of 1951), or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance 1956 (EB Ordinance No III of 1956) or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all order, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders passed in such suit, appeals applications and other legal Proceeding shall cease to have any effect; and no court shall entertain and no person shall bring fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question." 

 58. So after acquisition finally took place on the background of the gazette notification, exhibits 7 and 9, and as per decision of the Appellate. Division as mentioned herein above it can be said with authority that it concluded plaintiff’s title to the suit land and no court passes any decree affecting the title of the plaintiff. 

 63. Now, as to the basis of SA khatian. 

 64. From the side of defendant No. 1 it appears that attested copy of SA khatian No.  63 was produced exhibit 'Ka' and RS khatian No.  506. Learned Judge disbelieved SA khatian exhibit 1 submitted by plaintiff as it is not tallied with the certified copy of the SA khatian produced from the side of defendant No.  1. We are of the view that learned Judge was totally on wrong premises as plaintiff not only produced certified copy but also in their statement stated that this SA khatian can be found from different departments of government and also from the Government and filed application for calling for the volume from concern Assistant Commissioner (land) of Gazipur whereupon the court passed order No.  68 dated 30-11-2009 as:— 

 65. The SA khatian exhibit-la' submitted from the government custody and the SA khatian submitted from the plaintiffs custody, exhibit -1 are of the same and the same was recorded in the joint names of Chan Miah and Basor Uddin citing them as owners of the 'Ka' schedule suit property in equal II, anas owner each. From the judgment of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985, it is found that the present defendant No.  1 Deity had submitted SA Khatian No.  63 before the court claiming to have recorded in its name as owner. But here in this case, he with-held the said SA khatian and had submitted an information slip exhibit 'kha(1)1 stating that the SA khatian remained in the record room of DC office was turned of for the reason best known to him without explaing whatsoever about the previous exhibited SA khatian No.  63 in Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985. In such circumstances, it can easily be concluded that since the attested true copy of the SA khatian No.  63, exhibit-'Ka" submitted from the government custody and since the government had admitted in their written statements that the SA khatian No.  63 was prepared and published in the joint names of than Miah and Basor Uddin in equal share and since the said SA khatian exhibit `Ka' and the SA khatian of the plaintiffs, exhibit-1 are of the same and since the SA khatian prepared in the name of Chan Miah and Basor Uddin has got the basis i.e. exhibits-4 to 9, the plea of defendant Nos.  1 and 14 that the SA khatian was prepared in the name of defendant No.  1 is forged and fraudulent is not correct finding, rather we can come to the conclusion that the SA khatian, exhibit-1 was duly and correctly prepared and published in the name of Chan Miah and Basor Uddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs. Moreover, the finding of the previous suit regarding SA khatian prepared in the name of Chan Mian and plaintiffs' predecessor Basor Uddin is not binding upon the plaintiffs as the present plainiffs were not party in the previous Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985. 

 66. As such it may be reasonably presumed that defendant No.  1 intentionally produce distorted certified copy of SA khatian which learned Judge failed to consider and the finding of the learned Judge is totally beyond pleading of the parties. 

 67. Exhibits 7 and 9 published under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act with reference to particular estates, taluks, tenures, holding and tenancies and in respect of all rent receivers whose properties were under the management of Court of Wards Act, 1876. Sub-section 2(a) was enacted and introduced in section 3 of the Act by ordinance No.  111 of 1956. After this amendment, by general notification dated 2nd April, 1956 issued district wise in regard to all rent receiving interest which thereafter vested in the Government with effect from 14-4-56 in terms of those notification. As such, after 14-4-56 the defendant No.  1 has no right, title, interest or possession in itself what-ever it has, gone under the Government, not of it in any individual form to initiate any proceeding. A title less person has no legal character to initiate any proceeding. 

 70. Now, if we scrutinize the RS khatian No.  506, exhibit-12, we finds that same was recorded in the name of “ শ্রী মাধব বিগ্রহ সেবাইত দং সুরুজ বালা দেবী। বিভাবতি দেবী। জং কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী সাং নিজ।” The self same RS khatian was also filed by the defendant Nos.  1 and 14 claiming to have been correctly prepared and published in the name of defendant No.  1, Bigraha marking the same as exhibit Ka(1). In this respect the DW-1, Assistant Manager, Court of Wards of Bhawal Raj Estate stated in his deposition as follows:— 

 71. From the aforesaid statements made in cross-examination it is found that the DW-1 at one time claims that the 'Ka' schedule property is owned by the Court of Wards and at another time claims that the suit property is owned by the Deity, the defendant No.  1. At one stage, the DW-1 admitted that it had no basis for recording the name of Deity in the RS khatian. The two woman Shebayets as cited in the RS khatian had left the then East Pakistan now Bangladesh before Division of Pakistan and India. So the RS record prepared and published in the name of defendant Nod, Bigraha represented by two women as shebayets in equal II. Eight anas share as possessors is admittedly baseless and without foundation and, as such, the plaintiffs-appellants are entitled to have the relief against the said RS record as prayed for in his plaint as wrong, illegal, without any basis and not binding upon the plaintiffs appellants. 

 76. Learned Judge on the question of SA khatian No.  63 holds that it cannot be relied but we find that defendant No.  1 produced SA khatian and to overcome said SA khatian, plaintiff filed application for calling volume for the concerned Assistant Commissioner (Land) office but court rejected the said application as such statement of the learned Deputy Attorney-General has no leg to stand. 

 77. On wholesale acquisition, rent receipts, learned Advocate for the appellant relied on the case reported in 27 DLR (AD) 109, wherein it is held that "Notification published in the official Gazette under sub-section (2) of section 43 is a conclusive proof of such publication and in consequence thereof section 72 bars Civil Court from entertaining any suit in respect of the preparation, signing and publication of a compensation assessment roll of any party thereof under Chapter V or Chapter VA or in respect of any entry in or omission from such Roll. Non-obstante clause such as "notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force" have the effect of abrogating the previous laws which are inconsistent therewith but not those which do not stand in conflict. 

 82. Thus we are of the view that the leave petitioner had no locus-standi to challenge the draft Mahanagar Survey Khatian as prepared in the name of the respective writ petitioners, at-least after publication of the gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956." learned Advocate next relied on the case of 14 MLR (AD) 401 where it is held that "The plaintiffs were never recognized as co-sharers and on the contrary the heirs of Jinnat Ali are in exclusive possession of the suit land since the time of the CS record and they have acquired good title by continuous adverse possession for over 12 years. The right title interest of the plaintiff and their predecessor to the suit land has been extinguished by ouster and hostile adverse possession." Learned Advocate on adverse possession relied on 13 MLR (AD) 329 where it is held that "The plaintiff-respondent who embraced Islam is found to have been in peaceful and uninterrupted possession adversely to the interest of all others for more than 12 years and thereby acquired good and indefeasible title to the suit property described in schedule B of the paint which was formerly their family debattar property. The family Deity was removed there from and consequently the suit property ceased to be debattar property. The High Court Division set-aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court and restored the judgment and decree of the trial court on the above findings which the apex court held perfectly justified. 

 85. Learned Advocate next relied on the cases of 61 DLR 635 and 32 DLR 252, on time limit for declaratory suit. Against record of right, learned Advocate relied on the case of 8 BLD 497 where it is held that " The law is now settled that against the wrong record of rights the person whose interest is affected by such wrong recording need not file suit questioning legality of the record of rights so prepared and finally published within 6 years from said date or from the date of knowledge of such wrong record of rights, but he is required to file the suit seeking declaration of title within six years from the date the person in whose name record has been wrongly prepared and finally published raises claim denying his claim on the basis of wrong record." On wrong record of right learned Advocate next relied on 9 MLR (AD) 82 where it is held that "Knowledge of wrong record of the right can be starting point of limitation and a litigant public even if aware of wrong record of a cord of right can wait and wait till his right is invaded by other side and his suit will be well within time if he institutes suit within six years from date when his right on suit property is denied and invaded." 

 92. From the aforesaid facts, evidences both oral and documentary and also law involved in the case we conclude that the entire 23.13 acre `Ka' schedule property was a probability property before SAT Act. 1950. So, the said 23.13 acre 'Ka' schedule property was duly recorded in the names of the then projas namely Chan Mian and Basaruddin in SA Khatian No.  63 (Exhibit-1) by operation of section 3 of the SAT Act, through publishing probability property Gazette (Exhibit-7) and also by PO 90 of 1972 the RS Khatian No.  506(Exhibit-12) recorded in the name of  শ্রী মাধব বিগ্রহ সেবাইত দং সুরুজ বালা দেবী। বিভাবতি দেবী। জং কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী সাং নিজ।” is baseless and without foundation, as such, the same is not binding upon the plaintiffs. The defendant No.  14, Court of Wards, Bhowal Raj Estate claiming as shebaiyet of defendant No.  1 and the defendant No.  15, Land Reform board had illegally evicted the plaintiffs appellants on 3-3-2008 and 5-3-2008 from the `Kha' schedule property violating the order of injunction passed by the High Court Division on 3-3-2008 in Civil Rule No.  132(FM) of 2008 and also during the pendency of Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 of the joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur and as such, the plaintiffs are entitled to recover the said dispossessed 'Kha(2)' schedule property as prayed for in their petition dated 10-7-2008. The plaintiffs appellants having proved their right, title and possession in the rest of the 'Kha' schedule property i.e, `Kha(1); 'Kha(3); 'Kha(4); 'Kha(5)' and Kha 6 schedule property are entitled to protect their said property by the decree of confirmation of possession and permanent injunction.

lawyer:
Mr. Yousuf Ali, D. A. G with Ms. Kamrunnahar Lipy, A.A.G with Ms. Israt Jahan, A.A.G with Mr. Billal Ahmed Majumder, A.A.G -------- For the appellant
Mr. Md. Sherder Abul Hossain with Mr. Md. Saiyedul Islam, Advocates --------For the respondents

Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Cumilla. ----- Defendant No.1-appellant.
Vs.
Md. Jamal Mia and others -------- Plaintiff-respondents.
full_judgment:
2. Material facts relevant for disposal of the appeal, briefly, are that the respondent No.1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 135 of 2010 in the court of the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Cumilla impleading the Government as defendant praying declaration of title in the suit land and to correct the wrong record of right stating, inter-alia, that one Minnat Ali was the original owner of 20 decimal of land of Dag No.526 and his name has been included in C.S. Khatian No.2 as unpermitted possessor in the remark column. Minnat Ali possessed the suit land as illegal occupant. He died leaving behind 8 sons and 2 daughters respectively. Thereafter his son Shamsu got the said land in question by way of amicable settlement and subsequently he gifted the same to the plaintiff on 29.01.2008 by registered Kabala No.557/08. Thereafter plaintiff has been possessing and enjoying the property in question by fishing by developing surrounding areas of the said land till date but at the time of R.S record, the suit land has been recorded in Khatian No.1 wrongly. The said land in question has never been possessed and controlled by the East Pakistan Government and as the value of the land has been increased now and accordingly he came to learn about the wrong record on 05.09.2009 and hence, the suit. 

 3. The Government defendant Nos. 1-3 entered appearance in the suit and filed written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint stating, inter-alia, the suit is misconceived, incompetent and not maintainable in law, the plaintiff has/had no right, title and possession over the suit land. The suit property originally belonged to Khawja Habibullah and others and the predecessor of the plaintiff, Minnat Ali took possession of the suit land without taking permission from the real owner, Khawja Habibullah and others before preparation of C.S. Khatian and possession Minnat Ali was also recorded in the comment column of C.S. Khatian No. 2 as illegal occupant. After publishing C.S. Khatian Minnat Ali, the predecessor of the plaintiff left the suit property with uncared condition and after abolishing the Jamindari system the suit land measuring 20 decimal under dag No. 526 and other land adjacent land became vested in the Government. The plaintiff filed the case on false averments and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr. Md. Yusuf Ali, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the appellant in the course of argument takes us through the evidence and materials on record and then submits that admittedly C.S khatian was recorded in the name of Bharot Samrat, S.A khatian, B.S khatian and R.S khatian were also recorded in the name of Deputy Commissioner, Cumilla on behalf of the then Pakistan Government now the Bangladesh Government and the Government is now possessing the suit land. He further submits that the claim of the plaintiff is that the predecessor of the plaintiff was an unauthorized possessor of the suit land and it is on record that after publishing C.S khatian in the name of Government the predecessor of the plaintiff Minnot Ali left the suit land keeping it as abandoned and since then he had no possession in the suit land and when the SAT Act came into force in the year 1950, suit land became the khas land and recorded in the name of the Government. The learned Deputy Attorney General further submits the trial court wrongly found that suit land was partitioned between the sons and daughters of Minnot Ali although the plaintiff could not submit any document regarding such partition. Since Minnot Ali had no title, the heirs of Minnot Ali Samsu Mia also had no title, so the transfer registered deed No.557 dated 29.01.2008 in favour of Zamal Mia executed by Samsu Mia has no legal basis and the said transfer has been done without any title and without any lawful authority whatsoever. He further submits as per C.S, S.A and B.S khatian, it is found that suit land is "nal" land and the Government is in possession over the suit land till date but the learned trial Judge wrongly found that the suit land is pond and the plaintiff used to farming fish. He further submits that the Defendant-Appellant in their written statement stated that so called registered deed No. 557 dated 29.01.2008 is forged, void and created and on going through the said deed it is evident that J.L. No, khatian No, quantum of land and Dag No, are not identical with C.S. S.A and B.S khatian. More so, there is only one witness in the said deed and the said witness is identifier also, which proves that it is a created forged deed although the learned trial court without considering all these vital aspects of the case from a correct angle gave wrong finding that heirs of Minnot Ali possessed the suit land without permission of the owner and after the death of Minnot Ali, his son Samsu Mia has been possessing the suit land and subsequently Samsu Mia gifted the suit land to his son Zamal Mia in spite of fact that Minnot Ali and his son Samsu Mia had no title in the suit land. Title less illegal owner cannot transfer the land to anybody by the registered deed and that registered deed is illegal and it has no value in the eye of law and as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. 

 9. Mr. Md. Sherder Abul Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff respondent, on the other hand , submits that it is admitted facts by both the parties that the suit property originally belonged to Khawja Habibullah and others and the predecessor of the plaintiff, Minnat Ali took possession of the suit land without taking permission from the real owner, Khawja Habibullah and others before preparation of C.S. Khatian and this possession was also recorded in the comment column of C.S. Khatian No. 2. That C.S. Khatian was finally published in the year of 1926 and since then the plaintiff successively maintaining possession till today which is evident from the subsequent S.A, R.S. and B.S Khatian. In all those Khatians in comment column it has been written that plaintiff's predecessor was in possession without permission. So at least after expiry of 12 years from 1926 Minnat Ali accrued adverse title in the suit land as per provision of Section 28 read with Article 142 of the Limitation Act. He further submits that the Section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provided the list of property which will retain by the Government and in that list there is no mention about the land which was recorded in the name of private persons in C.S. Khatian prepared under the provision of section 3.B(5) of Bengal Tenancy Act and it is apparent in the C.S. Khatian No. 2 that it was recorded in the name of Khawja Habibullah and others as owners, so the entry of S.A. record in the name of Deputy Collector on behalf of East Pakistan Government and the defendant could not say as to how and in what procedure the Government of East Pakistan accrued the ownership in the suit property either in their written statements or producing any scrap of document and as such, the entry of S.A. and R.S. Khatian are baseless. Finally, Mr. Sherder Abul Hossain submits, the defendant asserted in the written statements that after publication of C.S. Khatian Minnat Ali left the suit property with uncared condition for earning his livelihood, as such the Government became owner of the suit land. In this respect the defendants did not adduce any corroborative witness or evidence to substantiate their case. Moreover there is provision in section 92(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for acquiring title by the Government in any abandoned property by filing a Miscellaneous Case and finally publishing Gazette Notification and the said act was effected from 14.04.1956 and the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has no retrospective effect, so the claim of the defendant is beyond the purview of any law and as such the entry of S.A, R.S. and B.R.S. Khatian are wrong and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 15. On close perusal of the record, it is found that the suit property originally belonged to Khawja Habibullah and others and the predecessor of the plaintiff, Minnat Ali took possession of the suit land without taking permission from the real owner, Khawja Habibullah and others before preparation of C.S. Khatian and this possession was also recorded in the comment column of C.S. Khatian No. 2 and C.S. Khatian was finally published in the year of 1926 under the provision of Section 103(B)(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act and since then the plaintiff successively maintaining possession till today which is found from evidence and materials on record. Section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provided the list of property which will retain by the Government and in that list there is no mention about the land which was recorded in the private persons in C.S. Khatian prepared under the provision of Section 3.B(5) of Bengal Tenancy Act and it is apparent in the C.S. Khatian No. 2 that it was recorded in the name of Khawja Habibullah and other as owners so the entry of S.A. record in the name of Deputy Collector on behalf of East Pakistan Government and the defendant could not say as to how and in what procedure the Government of East Pakistan accrued the ownership in the suit property either in their written statements or producing any scrap of paper and as such the entry of the suit land in S.A. and B.S. Khatian are baseless. 

 16. The defendant-Government asserted in the written statements that after publication of C.S. Khatian Minnat Ali left the suit property and went away from the suit land for earning his livelihood and thus the Government became owner. In this respect the defendants did not adduce any corroborative witnesses or evidence to substantiate their case. Besides, there is provision in the Section 92(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for acquiring title by the Government in any abandoned property by filing a Miscellaneous Case and finally publishing Gazette Notification and the said act was effected from 14.04.1956 and the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has no retrospective effect, so the claim of the defendant is beyond the purview of any law as such the entry of the land in question in S.A, R.S. and B.R.S. Khatian are wrong and not binding upon the plaintiff-respondent. 

 17. It is found that the C.S. Khatian No. 2 was prepared in the name of Khawja Habibullah and others and Minnat Ali took possession of the suit land without their permission before publication of C.S. Khatian and the matter was noted in the C.S. Khatian No.2 and C.S. Khatian was published in the year of 1926 and Minnat Ali continued his possession within the Knowledge of the real owner Kawja Habibulla, as such after expiry of 12 years i.e. in the year of 1938 Minnat Ali accrued title and it is well settled that "In order to claim title by adverse possession it is incumbent upon a person to prove that he has been in continuous possession of the disputed property over the statutory period of 12 years. Ref. 49 DLR (AD) 61.

full_judgment:
3. In the writ petition, it was stated, inter alia, that respondent No.5, the Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited, as the petitioner filed Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 before the High Court Division impleading the Director, the Settlement Office and the Assistant Settlement Officer, all of Land Records and Survey, Tejgaon, Dhaka, appellant No.1 herein (hereinafter referred to as writ-petitioner No.1) and 18 others challenging the order dated 5-2-1989 passed in Appeal Case Nos. 34046 of 1984 to 34054 of 1984 heard analogously by way of review by the Assistant Settlement Officer to have been passed without lawful authority and was no legal effect and to declare the striking out the name of the writ-petitioner (the Capital Co-operative Housing Society) from the RS Khatian No.1600(DP) as illegal and without any basis and lawful authority and also to declare the inclusion of the names of respondent Nos. 3-21 (in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989) in the RS Khatian as fraudulent and without any basis. Subsequently, by filing a supplementary affidavit a prayer was added as to why the order dated 18-1-1989 passed by writ-respondent No.1 (a), the Settlement Officer be not declared to have been passed with-out lawful authority and was of no legal effect. 

 4. The case of the writ-respondent No.5 (in the instant writ petition) in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 was that the land recorded in CS Khatian Nos. 138 and 330 bearing Plot Nos.881, 890, 893, 894 with a total area of 9.46 acres land and plot Nos.878, 879 with an area of 2.86 acres land respectively within Mouza-Uttar Khan, formerly within Police Station-Keraniganj, now Police Station-Gulshan, Dhaka originally belonged to Sharafatullah who died leaving behind 4(four) sons named Abdur Rahman, Pokai, Nazimuddin, Faizuddin and one daughter named Jewar Bibi. Bhawal Raj Estate, superior landlord of the case land, got a rent decree against the said tenants for arrear of rents in respect of CS Khatian No.330 and put the decree into execution and auction purchased the lands of this khatian and got delivery of possession thereof on 20-2-1930 and the said landlord also got another decree in a title suit against the said tenants and filed an execution case for the realization of the decretal costs, attached and put the lands of CS Khatian No. 138 in Court sale, auction purchased the same and got delivery of possession thereof on 20-6-1940. Subsequently, the said landlord settled the lands of those two CS Khatians with one Rahmat Banu on 3-3-1943 and she also got her name recorded in the SA Khatian and as she was threatened to be dispossessed from the case lands, she filed Title Suit No.80 of 1965 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Dhaka for permanent injunction against the successors-in-interest of said Sharafatullah and the purchasers, but as eventually, she was dispossessed from the case land, she filed another suit being Title Suit No.9 of 1970 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title and for recovery of possession which was decreed in her favour and she got delivery of possession of the case land and later on, the said writ-petitioner purchased the entire lands from Rahmat Banu by a registered sale deed bearing No.10884 dated 24-3-1978 and got delivery of possession thereof. 

 8. Writ-petitioner No.2, purchased-"in-possession" from the successive heirs-in-interest of said Sharafatullah and their vendee was added as opposite party in Miscellaneous Case No.3439 of 1995 vide the order dated 8-10-1995. After receipt of the notices, all the parties concerned recorded in the said RS Khatian No. 1600(DP) and also respondent No.5 appeared in the said miscellaneous case and contested the same. After perusing the said four applications, order dated 5-2-1989 passed in the said nine appeals, the judgment passed in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 and hearing the parties, Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan, the Assistant Settlement Officer, vide his order dated 2-1-1996 passed in Miscellaneous Case No.439 of 1995 proposed to prepare the RS Khatian in the names of the successive heirs-in-interest of said Sharafatullah and the petitioners along with other purchasers in possession from them after deleting the names of said Rahmat Banu and Capital Co-operative Housing Society Ltd (writ-respondent No.5 in the instant writ petition) from draft RS Khatian No.1600 and on 4-1-1996 submitted his said proposal before respondent No.3 for approval. Respondent No.3 after consulting the records vide his order dated 5-4-1996 accepted/approved the said proposal of Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan and ordered preparation of the record of right in conformity with the approved proposal and directed him to carry out the said order. Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan, vide his order dated 25-4-1996 carried out the earlier order dated 5-4-1996 passed by respondent No.3 and prepared the final RS Khatian No. 1600 of Mouza-Uttarkhan, Police Station-Gulshan Dhaka in the name of the petitioners and other successive heirs-in-interest and the purchasers-in-possession from them under rule 32 of the Rules, 1955. Thereafter the said RS Khatian No. 1600 was published finally under Rule 33 of the Rules, 1955 and a certificate stating the fact of such final publication was made by the revenue officer under rule 34(1) thereof. And then in the official Gazette Notification dated 26-9-1996, a declaration under rule 34(2) of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 was made by the Government to the effect that the records of right of Mouza-Uttar Khan, Police Station-Gulshan, Dhaka was finally published under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Following the said Gazette Notification dated 26-9-1996, respondent No.1 vide Memo No. Bhu:Ma/Sha-3/ Bhu:U :Ka/20/94/234(123) dated 6-10-1996 directed all concerned persons including respondent No.2 to take necessary steps so that fixation of LD Taxes and other functioning in this regard were done on the basis of the said finally published RS Khatians and thereby RS Khatian No.1600 was acted upon. Respondent No.5 having failed in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989, tried to mislead and influence various authorities including the offices of respondent Nos. 1 and 2 with an intention to get extra procedural, extra statutorily and extra-judicial benefits and privileges and in course of his said improper attempts, respondent No. 2 vide his office Memo No. Prati:/21/97/576 dated 28-5-1997 passed order directing correction of the record of rights stating that an illegal order dated 25-4-1996 was passed for preparation of record of rights, when the matter was finally settled in appeal and preparation of record of rights was in the last stage of printing. The impugned Memo dated 28-5-1997 was issued without giving the writ-petitioners any chance to be heard, though the same was entirely prejudicial for them. Writ-petitioner No.2 and one Mosammat Mallika Begum being unofficially informed of the impugned order dated 28-5-1997 on 16-6-1997 submitted a memorandum to the State Minister for Land to cancel the same and the State Minister forwarded the said memorandum to writ-respondent No.2 with a direction to consult the matter with writ-petitioner No.2 who though met writ-respondent No.2, went in vain. There-after, writ-petitioner No.2 and said Mosammat Mallika Begum on 5-10-1997 submitted another memorandum to the State Minister of Land with the same prayer which was forwarded to writ-respondent No.1 vide Memo Bhu:Ma/Sha-2 (Prakalapo/17/97-503 dated 21-10-1997 with a direction for enquiry by the Director (Record), Land Record and Survey Directorate, but the said Memorandum has still been kept in abeyance. On 26-4-1998 the concerned officers visited the case land for further preparation of the record of rights thereof and they verbally informed the writ-petitioners that they were officially bound by the impugned order dated 28-5-1997 to prepare the said record of rights in accordance with the same. 

 13. Writ-petitioner No. 1 (appellant No.1) filed a supplementary affidavit stating, inter alia, that the original owner of the land of CS Khatian No.330 of Mouza 195, Uttar Khan under present Police Station-Uttar Khan was one Bholanath Singh and from whom Sharafatullah, son of late Robiullah became the owner and possessor under sthitiban rayoti title in respect of Plot Nos. 878, 879, 881, 890, 89. 994 measuring in total 12.32 acres land and the name of Sharafatullah was correctly recorded in CS Khatian Nos.138 and 330. After the death of CS recorded tenant, Sharafatullah, the name of one Rahmat Banu appeared in SA Khatian Nos. 239 and 434 in respect of the aforesaid 12.32 acres land appertaining to those six plots and, as such, the heirs of Sharafatullah at the time of last RS operation filed 9(nine) objection cases under rule 30 of the Rules, 1955 and those objection cases were allowed in part. Respondent No.5 (Capital Co-operative Housing Society Ltd) being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order passed in the aforesaid 9(nine) objection cases filed 9 (nine) appeals under Rule 31 of the Rules, 1955 bearing numbers: 34046-34054 of 1984 and on consideration of the papers and documents those appeals were finally dismissed on contest by the Assistant Settlement Officer, Dhaka Zone, Dhaka by his order dated 5-2-1989 with a direction to record the names of the objector appellants only in RS Khatian No.1600. As it appeared from annexure-' Ka', respondent No.5 settled the properties of SA Khatian Nos.239 and 434 covering 6 plots of original CS Khatian Nos.138 and 330 measuring 12.32 acres land by way of perpetual lease to 162 persons and after they lost in the settlement appeals under rule 31 being Nos.3446-3454 of 1948, filed Writ Petition No. 1080 of 1989 and obtained a Rule Nisi; the Rule Nisi issued in the aforesaid writ petition was discharged on 2-3-1993; Another Division Bench by its judgment and order dated 14-11-1991 in Writ Petition Nos.207 and 208 of 1989 dealing with more or less the same principle of law involved in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989, amongst others, declared that the Director General of Land Records could not exceed his power by entertaining and disposing of a second review petition against the order passed by the Settlement Officer in appellate jurisdiction in respect of correction of record of rights. Respondent No.5 did not challenge the judgment and order dated 2-3-1993 passed in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 before this Division and thus accepted the result of their above mentioned writ petition, but got a series of suits filed through their lessees before the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka impleading the writ-petitioners as defendant Nos.27 and 34 respectively and respondent No.5 as pro-forma defendant No.55. Writ-petitioner No.2 was contesting those suits by filing written statements and to the knowledge of the petitioners, respondent No.5 was giving active support and assistance to the plaintiffs of those ongoing title suits in which they challenged the Gazette being No. ভুঃ মঃ/শাঃ-২(গঃ বিঃ)-৭৪-৯৫-৩৯২ dated 24-9-1996 in respect of RS Khatian No. 1600 more or less attracting the subject matter of the writ petition. 

 "Mr. Rokonuddin Mahmud, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners submit-ted that after preparation and final publication and gazette notification of khatian on completion of all legal requirements as provided in State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 there was no scope for the respondent No.2 to reopen the issue on any pretext and in these circumstances, the High Court Division seriously erred in law in holding that the impugned memo is merely a communication from one office to another to perform certain official acts and committed gross injustice in discharging the Rule on the ground of maintainability alone without going to the merit of the case; that after publication of the official gazette notification under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 read with Rule 34(2) of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955, the record of right is to be presumed to be correct under Rule 35 of the said State Acquisition Rules which can only be declared incorrect by the competent memo issued by the respondent No.2 is without jurisdiction and is liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect; that all the necessary parties were made parties in the writ petition and, as such, the case law referred to by the High Court Division are not applicable in the present case. The learned Counsel further submitted that having regard to the provision of rule 42 of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 which vested the Revenue Officer appointed with additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' with the power to direct cancellation of any portion of the proceedings referred to in rules 28 to 30 in respect of any district or part of a district or local area at any time before publication of the final record of rights, the High Court Division was wrong in failing to hold that the impugned order passed by the respondent No.2 after publication of the gazette notification dated 24-9-1999 under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, which is final, directing the Settlement Officer to correct the record of right in favour of respondent No.5 upon finding that the direction dated 24-4-1996 to publish the record of rights in the name of the petitioner and others, ultra vires, the provision of the said rule 42 and is without lawful authority, arbitrary and malafide." 

 19. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the High Court Division discharged the Rule Nisi on the findings, inter alia, that: (i) The interest of the writ-petitioners (there were two writ-petitioners) in the case land was not stated in the writ petition; it was not clear what quantum of land belonged to each of them "singularly and/or jointly" and how they would be aggrieved if the survey records were amended pursuant to the impugned Memo; (ii) the impugned memo did not contain any quantum of land or mention any specific plot number or khatian number except referring to the land "as that recorded in the name of Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited in Mouza-Uttar Khan"; (iii) the occupants and the owners of the land in question had not been made parties, if the Rule Nisi was made absolute as prayed for by the appellants, then all the persons in possession of the concerned land and the persons who claimed title thereof would be adversely affected. They also had a right to be heard before any order could be passed affecting their interest in the land, no one except certain officials connected with the Land Record and Survey and Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited represented by its Chairman were made respondents; (iv) the appellants impugned memo No.Prati:21/97/576 dated 28-5-1997 issued under the signature of writ-respondent No.2, Director General, Directorate of Land Record and Survey, Tejgaon, Dhaka addressed to the Settlement Officer. Dhaka regarding correction of records in Mouza-Uttar Khan in the name of Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited stating that the land survey records prepared as per rules in the name of Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited was at the last stage for publication; that after hearing the appeal through an illegal order dated 25-4-1996 under rule 42 of the Rules, 1955, an order was passed for recording the said land in the name of some other persons; the Director General, Land Records and Survey, after enquiry found the said order illegal and gave direction for correction of the survey records as per the rules; (v) the impugned Memo was merely a communication from one office to another to perform certain official acts and that was not acted upon.

lawyer:
