AB Roy Chowdhury, Advocate—For Opposite parties in both cases.
parties:
Balai Chandra Saha and others ------ Petitioners
VS
Sukumar Chakroborty and others --------- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
4. The case of the plaintiffs of Other Class Suit No. 67 of 1987 was that 0.52 acre land was originally belonged to Gopinath Sharma to the extent of 12 anna share and Katayani Debi to the extent of 4 anna share and accordingly, CS Khatian was prepared and finally published in their name. While Katayani Debi was owning and possessing her 4 anna share i.e 0.13 acre land, died without any issue and leaving behind Gopinath Sharma as the elder brother of her husband and accordingly, he inherited the share of Katayani Debi and thereafter, he died leaving behind Harigobinda Chakraborty as his only son to inherit his share and Harigobinda Chakraborty while was owning and possessing said 0.52 acre land died leaving behind two sons, the plaintiffs to inherit his share. Having inherited entire 0.52 acre land of suit plot, the plaintiffs have been owning and possessing the same by constructing dwelling house, planting various types of tress and producing crops therein. The plaintiffs, subsequently, came to know that SA kahtian had been wrongly prepared and published in the name of Biraja Sundari Daisya and accordingly, they instituted Other Class Suit No. 100 of 1986 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Bajitpur, Kishoreganj praying for declaration that SA record was wrong and then got ex-parte decree against Biraja Sundari Daisya. The residential house of the defendant situates just adjacent to the eastern side of suit plot and they forcefully dispossessed the plaintiffs from 0.03 acre land out of 0.52 acre land on 30-6-1978 corresponding to 15th Baishak, 1394 BS by erecting cowshed therein and, as such, they have constrained to institute the suit. 

 6. The case of the defendant-petitioners (plaintiff of Other Class Suit No. 80 of 1987) is that 0.52 acre land was originally belonged to Gopinath Sharma to the extent of 12 anna share and Katayani Debi to the extent of 4 anna share as rioti Jote right and CS kahtian was prepared and published in their names. Katayani Debi then transferred her share by a pattan dated 5th Baishakh, 1361 BS to Biroja Sundary Daisya and handed over possession thereof to her and while Biraja Sundari Daisya was owning and possessing said 0.13 acre land, SA kahtian was prepared and finally published in her name jointly with the plaintiffs without any objection from any quarter. Biroja Sundary Daisya brought her daughter namely, Horidashi Saha and her husband Amar Chandra Saha in her own house and transferred said 0.13 acre land by way of oral gift in favour of them and handed over possession thereof to them. Thereafter, she died leaving behind one daughter Horidashi Saha and one grandson, Direndra Chandra Saha (son of her deceased daughter Roydashi). Thereafter, Horidashi and her husband Amar Chandra Saha transferred said land to Balai Chandra Saha (the defendant No. 1) vide registered sale deed dated 28-4-1969 being No. 2113 and handed over possession thereof to him and after purchase, Balai Chandra Saha mutated his name in the revenue office of the Government and had been owning and possessing the same by paying rents to the Government. Thereafter, Dhirendra Chandra Saha claimed title over 0.13 acre land for which Balai Chandra Saha again purchased the same from Dhirendra Chandra Saha vide registered sale deed dated 6-2-1982 being No. 780 for avoiding future complications. 

 7. His further case was that during BS operation said land was recorded in his name in field survey and bujarat khatian was prepared in his name against which the plaintiffs, Sukumar and Sudeb, filed objection case and the same was rejected and then they filed appeal under Rule 30 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules and the appeal officer, after considering oral and documentary evidence, dismissed the appeal vide order dated 15-2-1987. The plaintiffs of Other Class Suit No. 67 of 1987 by collusion and fraud obtained ex-parte decree in Other Class Suit No. 100 of 1987 against dead person because the defendant of that suit, Biroja Sundari Daisya, was not alive at the time of filing of the suit. 

 13. Learned Advocate further submits that, upon sifting the evidence on record, the trial Court found that though Balai Chandra Saha could not prove pattan and oral gift but he have continuous possession of the suit property since his predecessors, in that after transfer by Katayani Debi SA record was prepared and finally published in the name of the transferee, Biroja Sundari and after purchase from her, Balai Chandra Saha mutated his name in the Government revenue office and paid rent and accordingly, Balai Chandra Saha acquired title in the suit land. Learned Advocate further submits that though Sukumar .Chandra Chakraborty and Sudeb Chandra Chakraborty claimed title over 0.13 acre suit land but they could not produce any single paper or document to show that they were in possession of the suit land inasmuch as they or their predecessors could not record their names in the SA or BS Khatian and could not mutate their names in respect of said 0.13 acre land and did not pay any rent to the Government and accordingly, their right, title or possession ,have not been established by oral and documentary evidence but the appellate Court without considering the case of the parties side by side or discussing the evidence independently, came to a wrong conclusion that Sukumar Chandra Chakraborty and Sudeb Chandra Chakraborty acquired title in respect of 0.13 acre land. 

 18. It is admitted by both parties that 0.52 acre land was originally owned and possessed by Gopinath Chandra Sharma to the extent of 12 anna share and Katayani Debi to the extent of 4 anna sharre as royoti jote holders and accordingly, said land was recorded and finally published in CS Khatian No. 550 (Exhibit-1) of CS plot No. 2157 in their name to the extent of their respective share. The plaintiffs of Other Class Suit No. 67 of 1987 claimed that Katayani Debi held her share as ayautaka stridhana and after her death, said land was inherited by her husband's elder brother Gopinath Chandra Sharma as per section 157 of Mulla's Principle of Hindu Law, 14th Edition. In their pleadings, the plaintiffs did not plead that said land was ayutuka stridhana. However, the trial Court, upon taking that said property as ayautaka stridhana of Katayani Debi, found that as per section 157 of Mulla's Hindu Law only husband's younger brother inherits ayautaka stridhana and accordingly, Gopinath Chandra Sharma, being the elder brother of the husband of Katayani Debi did not inherit said land and as heirs of Gopinath Chandra Sharma, Sukumar and Sudeb did not acquire any right, title or interest in the suit property. On perusal of section 157 of Mulla's Hindu Law, appears that on the death of a Hindu widow her ayautaka stridhana devolves upon the following heirs: 

 23. The claim of Balai Chandra Saha is that Katayani Debi, while owning and possessing .13 acre land, transferred the same to Biroja Sundari Dasya by jote pattan dated 5th Baishakh, 1361 BS and while she was owning and possessing the same, SA Khatian No. 727 (Exhibit-l ka) was prepared and finally published in her name and thereafter, she transferred the same to her daughter Haridashi Saha and son-in-law Amar Chandra by way of oral gift and then they, by registered sale deed dated 28-4-1969 being No. 2113 (Exhibit-Ga), transferred the same to Balai Chandra Saha (plaintiff of Other Class Suit No. 80/87) and being owner in possession he mutated his name in the revenue office vide Mutation Case No. 1329 (IX-DP of 75-76.and got DCR (Exhibit-Ka) and was owning and possessing the same on payment of rents (Exhibits ka series) and said land was also recorded in his name in BS Jarip in Bujarat khatian No. 58 and DP khatian No. 1939 in plot No. 4075. His further case is that Sukumar and Sudeb filed objection against said Bujarat Khatian which was rejected and thereafter, they filed appeal under Rule 30 of the SAT Rules and after hearing, said appeal was dismissed vide judgment dated 15-2-1987 (Exhibit-kha). It is also claimed that Biroja Sundary had another daughter namely, Roydashi and when her son Dhirendra Chandra Roy claimed said 0.13 acre land, Balai Chandra Saha got sale deed registered from Dhirendra Chandra Roy being No. 780 dated 6-2-1982 (Exhibit. Gha) in respect of said 0.13 acre land for avoiding future complications. 

 25. The plaintiffs of Other Class Suit No. 67 of 1987 could not prove by evidence that those two sale deeds of 1969 and 1982, SA khatian, mutation of Balai, rent receipts and BS record in the name of Balai Chandra as forged or collusive. 

 26. On perusal of order dated 15-2-1987 passed by the settlement officer in appeal, it appears that during BS field survey said 0.13 acre land was recorded in Bujarat khatian No. 58 in BS plot No. 4075 in the name of Balai Chandra against which Sukumar and Sudeb filed objection and the same was rejected and accordingly, DP khatian No. 1939 was published in the name of Balai Chandra. It also reveals that against said DP khatian, Sukumar and Sudeb filea appeal under Rule 30 of the SAT Rules and during hearing of said appeal Sukumar adduced Sudhendra Chandra Roy as witness who, on 10-2-1987, deposed that Balai forcefully entered into possession in said 0.13 acre land in the month of Magh of previous year. On 15-2-1987 Sukumar adduced (1) Dhirendra Chandra Banik, (2) Omesh Chandra Banik, (3) Md Manu Mia and (4) Mujibuddoulla as witnesses out of whom Dhirendra and Omesh stated that dispute suit was continuing for 2/3 years and before 2/3 years back appellant was in possession in the suit land. Manu Mia stated that dispute was continuing between the parties in regards possession for 4/5 years and Mujibuddoula stated that dispute was continuing between the parties for 7/8 years. It appears the witnesses made contradictory statements in regards possession of the appellants before the appeal officer. On the other hand, Balai Chandra adduced (1) Md Mahram Ali (2) Md Jadu Mia and (3) Khurshid Mia as witness who, stated that Balai Chandra has been owning and possessing the suit land since 1969 and before that Biroja Sundari was in possession thereof. The settlement officer, after considering oral and documentary evidence like SA khatian, sale deeds, rents receipts, found that after purchase in 1969 Balai Chandra mutated his name vide mutation case of 1975-76 and paid rents up to 1390 BS and also observed that the appellants (plaintiffs of Other Class Suit No. 67 of 1987) could not prove their possession thereof and the opposite party Balai Chandra could prove his possession in the suit land and accordingly, dismissed the appeal. It appears that the opposite parties did not challenge said order of the settlement officer before any higher forum. 

 28. It appears that Balai Chandra, during trial, could not produce pattan dated 5th Baishakh, 1361 BS executed by Katayani Debi to Biroja Sundari during trial but produced the same before this Court for considering it as additional evidence. It appears that the document (Annexure A) is an unregistered private document and, as such, it cannot be taken as additional evidence in revision by this Court without proof of its genuineness by proving its execution by evidence. Though the defendants could not prove the pattan and oral gift by Biroja Sundari to her daughter Hari Dasi and Amar Chandra but chronological facts of publication of SA khatian in the name of Biroja Sundari in respect of 0.13 acre land, transfer of said land by Hari Dasi and Amar Chandra to Balai Chandra by registered sale deed dated 6-2-1969, mutation of said land in the year 1975 in the name of Balai, payment of rents by him to the Government and subsequent preparation of BS khatian in his name suggest that, Balai Chandra Saha had been possessing said 0.13 acre land from the time of his predecessor Biroja Sundari against said Sukumar and Sudeb and their predecessors uninterruptedly for more than 12 years and accordingly, he has acquired title by way of adverse possession against them. Accordingly, the trial Court rightly held that Balai Chandra could able to prove his title and possession in the suit land. 

 30. On perusal of ex-parte order and decree dated 12-4-1987 of Other. Class Suit No. 100 of 1986 [Exhibits 2(ka) and 2(kha)] it appears that said suit was filed by Sukumar and Sudeb on 15-11-1986 against Biroja Sundari challenging SA khatian prepared and published in her name and got ex-parte decree against her. On sifting evidence of the parties, the trial Court found that Biroja Sundari died before filing of the suit and, as such, the decree which was passed against dead person is a nullity in the eye of law. 

 32. Now, question arises whether, Balai Chandra Saha has got any right to challenge the ex-parte decree or whether he was a necessary party to that suit. PW 1 Sudeb Chakraborty, in his cross-examination recorded on 6-11-1990, stated that 6 year back he learnt that RoR was wrongly prepared in the name of Biroja Sundari when he had gone to CO office for payment of rent and before that the defendants mutated their names but he did not file any case for cancellation of the mutation. He also stated that field record was prepared in the name of Balai against which they filed objection case under rule 30. Admittedly, the plaintiffs lost therein on contest. The testimony of PW 1 suggests that before filing of OC Suit No. 100 of 1986 Sukumar and his brother knew that Balai Chandra got his name mutated in the SA khatian in place of Biroja Sundari and was paying rents to the revenue office. After mutation from SA recorded tenant Biroja Sundari, Balai Chandra stepped into her shoes and thus, acquired subsisting interest in the suit jote. Moreover, during resent BS operation, the suit land was recorded in BS DP Khatian No. 1939, on contest, in the name of Balai Chandra Saha. Accordingly, he was a necessary party in OC Suit No. 100 of 1986. The suit, which has been filed against his predecessor-in-interest was bad for defect of parties and is not binding upon him and, as such, he has got every right to challenge said ex-parte decree passed therein. Accordingly, the finding of the appellate Court that Balai Chandra have got no authority to challenge the ex-parte decree is misconceived and not tenable in law.

full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the appellant herein and others as plain-tiffs filed Other Class Suit No.131 of 1997 before the Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram for partition. They contended, inter alia, that the land described in the schedule to the plaint has been finally published in R.S. Khatian No.291 with the name of Anu Mia being an owner of the properties, who sold 44 decimal land to Ashu Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs by registered deed No.724 dated 31.01.1954. The plaintiffs obtained total 58% decimal land and have been owning and possessing the suit land. The defendants have no right, title and interest in the suit land of the plaintiffs. On 19.09.1997 when the defendants denied to partition the said land from the jote, the cause of action arose and hence, the plain-tiffs filed the suit. 

 "I. That the petitioner did not seek partition of the tank which is in Khatian No.202 in Plot Nos.124, 125, 131 and on receiving the written statement, made it clear by an amendment of the plaint that the tank has not been incorporated in the schedule of the plaint as it has been peacefully possessed by the co-sharers jointly and the appellate Court by misreading of those arrived at a finding that all the co-sharers have not been impleaded in the suit and observed “বিবাদী পক্ষে কথিত ২০২ নং খতিয়ানে ১২৪/১২৫/১৩১ দাগে ভূমি জলে পড়ে দিঘী। এখানে ২০০ জনের উপরে শরীক আছে। দিঘীর পরিমান ১০—কানি। আছু মিঞার অন্দরে ভূমি পরিমাণ ৩—গন্ডা বাকী সম জোতের উক্ত শরীকগণকে পক্ষ করেননি বলে অত্র আদালতে বিবেচনায় মূল মোকদ্দমা পক্ষভাবে দোষে দুষ্ট হবে।”and the High Court Division committed an error of law in not considering the fact that the finding of the appellate Court is perverse, which affected the merit of the case. II. That the appellate Court further observed in its finding that 

 6. Mr. Abdus Sobhan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. In addition the learned Advocate submitted that the evidence on record itself speaks that one Anu Mia originally owned and possessed the property in schedule No.1 and the R.S. record of rights khatian No.291 was finally published, (Exhibit 2 Series) and the property of schedule No.2 also belonged to Anu Mia and others whose names appear in the R.S. record of rights finally published (Exhibit-2 Series) and who sold 44 decimals land to the predecessors of the plaintiff by deed No.724 registered on 04.02.1954 (Exhibit-3) and the plaintiffs produced B.S. Khatian No. 254 (C.C) and Asu Mia Majhi, predecessor of the plain-tiffs also purchased 141/3 decimals land by Exhibit-3 from Plot Nos.106/115/112 shown in schedule No.2 and in such a way the plaintiffs owned and are possessing 44 + 14 1/3 = 581/3 decimals land in both the schedules and sought partition and the High Court Division by misreading of those erroneously affirmed the finding of the appellate Court. He submitted that the predecessor of the plaintiffs and subsequently the plaintiffs themselves are in possession of the said quantum of land by virtue of the said sale deed (Exhibit-3) and the record of rights (Exhibit-2 series) on payment of usual taxes to the government, and in such circumstances the finding of possession of the, Court of first appeal was made through inadvertence and the High Court Division committed an error of law to give emphasis of the finding of possession of the Court on first appeal without considering the relevant aspects of possession. 

 9. There was a claim and counter claim with regard to the fraction/share of land mentioned iii the schedule of deed No.724 registered on 04.2.1954. On direction from this Court the original volume containing the deed in question was transmit-ted to this Court by the (office of the District Registrar, Chattogram. On perusal of the volume and the deed in question, it transpires that the deed was created by Anu Miah Majhi, in favour of Asu Mia Majhi on 31.01.1954 and registered on 04.2.1954. The quantum of land sold is in total 58 1/3 decimals. Out of that lad, the disputed quantum of 44 decimals of R.S. Khatian No.291 is under the scanner. 

 11. The defendants claim that in the second schedule to the deed registered on 04.02.1954 the total land is 46 decimals of which the plaintiffs claim 1/3 that is 14 1/3 decimals. In the same way the predecessor of the defendants sold only 1/3 of the total land of khatian No. 291 that is 22 decimals out of total 66 decimals. Hence, the plaintiffs claim to title over remaining 44 decimals is false. 

 13. In his deposition defendant No.1 deposing as D.W.1 stated that in R.S. khatian No. 291 from plot Nos. 131, 132,133 and 101 his father sold only 1/3, i.e. 22 decimals by deed No. 724, and the plaintiffs have no claim to the remaining 44 decimals land. The trial Court accepted that the plaintiffs claim to title over 5873 decimals land is supported by the kabala Ext.3. On the other hand, the appellate Court observed that the schedule in the sale deed is self-contradictory because the plaintiffs' predecessor purchased only 'hot' the land detailed in the schedule 1 of the deed and, therefore, they could claim only 22 decimals land out of 66 decimals. It was also observed that in the B.S. khatian it is stated that the land sold is 1/3. The appellate Court also found defect of party and hotchpot.

Jannatul Maowa Runa and others ------------ Petitioners 
Vs.

full_judgment:
6. Per contra, the present-petitioner as pre-emptee-purchaser contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegations so made in the petition for pre-emption contending, inter alia, that, one Akbar Ali had been in possession over 30 decimals of land on mutating his name in the khatian and while he had been enjoying title and possession over that 30 decimals of land he at first proposed the pre-emptor to sell the case land even the father of the pre-emptees named, Nazrul Islam also proposed the pre-emptor and his son to purchase the land but as they refused to purchase the same, the pre-emptees then purchased the case land by registered kabala dated 11-9-2001. Soon after purchasing the case land, the pre-emptees then started enjoying title and possession over the suit properties by planting various trees that cost Taka 65,000. It has further been stated that, there has been a Madrasha located in the case land though it was not made party in the case. It has then stated that, the vendor, Korban Ali who transferred 5 decimals of land upon purchasing 10 decimals of land had separated his jama before selling 5 decimals of land to the pre-emptor. It has stated in the written objection that, inspite of having no preferential right the pre-emptor filed the case having absolute knowledge about the disputed transfer. It has further been stated that, if the pre-emption case is allowed in that event, the pre-emptee Nos. 1-3 will suffer irreparable loss and injury and therefore the pre-emption case is liable to be dismissed. 

 15. By filing two supplementary-affidavits, the petitioners also produced the registered kabala dated 26-11-1997 and registered kabala dated 11- 9-2001, a filed porcha bearing khatian No. 721 appertaining to plot No. 629 standing in the name of the pre-emptees-petitioners in respect of 17 decimals of land. By filing another supplementary-affidavit dated 22-11-2017, the petitioners also annexed some documents which were marked as exhibits `E1 -E2.' In another supplementary-affidavit the pre-emptees-petitioners also produced a registered kabala dated 15-7-2001 through which 20 decimals of land was transferred by the son of the pre-emptor in favour of the opposite party No. 1 Akbar Ali. 

 16. In support of submission, the learned Counsel has then placed his reliance in a slew of decisions reported in 19 DLR 510, 33 DLR (HC) 18, 50 DLR (AD) 97, 17 BLD 513, 12 BLC (HC) 787, 42 DLR (AD) 189, 32 DLR (AD) 55. With such submission, and relying on those decisions, the learned Counsel finally prays for making the Rule absolute on setting aside the concurrent judgement and order passed by the learned Judges of the courts below. 

 19. The learned Counsel further submits that, since under the provision of clause (C) of section 117(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act there has been gulf of difference between separation of holding and separation of jama so mere mutating the name in the khatian by the predecessor of the present-pre-emptors will not deprive the pre-emptor to exercise his statutory right of pre-emption to pre-empt the case land. 

 20. The learned Counsel further submits that. though the pre-emptees in its written objection allegedly stated that, before selling 5 decimals of land in favour of the pre-emptor by Korban Ali, he had mutated his name in the khatian vide mutation case but nothing of that sort of document has ever been produced by the said pre-emptees during the process of taking evidence so it clearly shows that, the mutation proceedings so have been alleged by the pre-emptees-petitioners has got no existence in the eye of law. 

 21. The learned Counsel further submits that, though it is alleged by the pre-emptees that, subsequent record has been prepared in the name of the pre-emptees in respect of case land, but from the record it cannot show that, the said record has finally been published in the name of the pre-emptees so until and unless a record is finally published, in that event, is cannot be said that, the holding has been separated or it recorded in the name of the pre-emptees resulting in it cannot be held that the pre-emptees have been holding possession in separate portion of land by splitting up the holding in which the pre-emptor filed the instant pre-emption case. 

 24. With such submission and relying on those decisions, the learned Counsel finally prays for discharging the Rule. 

 27. Now, only point remains, whether the pre-emptor ceased to have any right as a co-sharer by purchase to have the case land by way of purchase. It is alleged by the pre-emptees that, the vendor that is, Korban Ali before transferring 5 decimals of land infavour of the pre-emptees mutated his name in the khatian vide mutation case No. 2762 (9-1) 86/87 dated 11-11-1987 so before transferring the said case land, the khatian since has been spitted up so the pre-emptor cannot claim to be a co-sharer by purchase in the case holding. It has further been claimed by the pre-emptees that, after purchasing the case land even they also mutated their respective name in the khatian vide Mutation Case Nos. 1250, 1251 and 1252 in the year 2001 and 2002. Though there has been no mutation case number ever stated in the written objection but OPW 1 who is the father of pre-emptee purchaser No. 1 and 3 and the father in-law of the pre-emptee No. 2 has deposed that, in the month of March 2002 they got their names mutated in the khatian. 

 29. Now, for argument sake, had the vendor of the pre-emptee ever mutated his name, in that event whether the pre-emptor would have barred in exercising his right to pre-empt the case land or not. It is the contention of learned Counsel for the opposite party that, mere mutating the name in the khatian will never deprive the pre-emptor to exercise his right of pre-emption. In countenance of his submission, the learned Counsel has placed his reliance in the decision so have been reported in 3 ALR 58, which is propounded here: 

 31. To substantiate that very submission, the learned Counsel has also placed his reliance in the decision reported in 18 BLT (HC) 83 where it has clearly been held that, as regards to point of law, the later decisions will always prevail over. Though in the decision reported in 3 ALR 58. the decision so have been given by the Hon'ble Appellate Division on that particular point made under section 117(C) has not been referred even though I find substance in it because in all along the subsequent decision always prevails over. And in the decision reported in 3 ALR it has vividly been discussed how a separation of jama and a separation of holding can be distinguished. Because, under the provision of clause (C) of section 117(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, if any-person wants to separate a holding, in that event several procedure has to be performed but in the process of separating a jama which is generally called mutation in the khatian an application is simply filed before the respective Tohsil Office who then refers the same to the Assistant Commissioner (land) and the Assistant Commissioner land upon performing some procedure just mutates the khatian enabling the applicant to pay the rent in respect of his portion of land by which it cannot be said that separation of holding is held. Moreover, in separating a holding there must have some procedure to be carried out by issuing notice to all the co-sharer of the case holding but nothing of this sort has ever been complied with in the instant case. 

 35. Now let me asses the contention made in two supplementary-affidavits so submitted by the learned Counsel for the petitioner one, at the time of issuance of the Rule and another, on 22-11-2017. By way of first supplementary-affidavit dated 7-2-2013 the petitioners have produced two deeds dated 26-11-1997, 11-9-2001, the khatian No. 437 when the survey reached at the stage of DP and that of the field porcha (মাঠ পর্চা) with regard to khatian No. 721 appertaining to plot No. 629 stands in the name of the present pre-emptees-petitioners. By filing those documents, the learned Counsel for the petitioners tried to give emphasis on the point that, since the present khatian number is different from that of the purchased deed of the pre-emptor dated 26-11-1997 and 11-9-2001 where the recent plot number has been mentioned as 435 and 437 so the khatian has already been changed so the pre-emptor has ceased to have any right to pre-empt the case land for having enjoyed the land that fails in separate khatian. In order to give emphasis to that, the learned Counsel has also placed his reliance in DP khatian No. 437 which has also been marked as exhibit-D-1 and that of (মাঠ পর্চা) appertaining to khatian No. 721 which has been marked as Annexure-E to the supplementary-affidavit filed on 7-12-2013. 

 36. Anyway, I have very meticulously gone through all those documents but I don't find any iota of substance in those documents because from those documents it does not show the said khatians have finally been published in the name of the pre-emptor or that of the name of the pre-emptees. And in that regard, the learned Counsel for the opposite party has placed his reliance on the decision reported in 36 DLR 193 where it has been held that; 

 37. It has already been held that, in absence of final publication of record of right as provided in section 19 and section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act there cannot be any presumption as to the correctness. In such a view, it can safely construe that, until and unless a khatian is finally published, the pre-emptee cannot claim to have separated the holding, so that very decision is squarely applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. 

 41. So only point is left for the pre-emptee-petitioners that, the pre-emptor has ceased to be any co-sharer in the case holding but no documents haw produced which will suffice to prove the said assertion. Because, though in the written objection the pre-emptees claimed that, before being transferred 5 decimals of land by the vendors of the pre-emptor, he mutated his name in the khatian mentioning a certain mutation case number but nothing of that sort document has been produced to that effect. 

 42. Moreover, it has already been decided by our Apex Court that, mere mutating the name in the khatian will not deprive or will not cease the right of the pre-emptor in exercising its statutory right of pre-emption.

full_judgment:
2. Respondent Nos.1-6 as plaintiffs instituted other Class suit No. 235 of 83 in the Court of subordinate Judge, Rajshahi for decree of declaration of their right and title in the Kha schedule property against the defendants stating that the schedule 'Ka' land of the plaint was owned by late Majnani Bewa. The suit lot-I property was under her Khas possession, while the 1st-2 property was enjoyed by her by granting Korfa Patton and the land was recorded in C.S. Khatian in her name accordingly. The property in 1st-1 was shown as her own property, while 1st-2 property was recorded showing under possession of Korfa tenants in Khatian Nos. 1538, 1550. One of the Korfa tenants Ibrahim Mollah surrendered his Korfa right to the original land lady Manjony Bewa and the other Korfa tenants abandoned the property and it was resumed by the owner Manjony Bewa as her Khas possession and was enjoyed by her. In the year of 1936 by oral, gift she transferred entire property to one Monir son of her sister, who was also a son of her husband's brother Syed Ali Mollah. At the time of her death Syed Ali Mollah was a minor and Ibrahim Mollah used to look after the property of Monir Syed Ali Mollah. Manjony Bewa and Sajen Bewa were full sisters and the father of Monir gamed Syed Ali month was husband's brother of Manjony Bewa Manjony died 'issueless' and on the death of Manjony Bewa and Ibrahim Mollah, Syed Ali Mollah became the owner in possession of the Kha schedule property under Khatian No. 1539 by way of gift and also by way of inheritance from his father and mother. After the death of Ibrahim Mollah, Syed Ali Mollah married a nice of Ibrahim Mondal of the locality. Ibrahim Mondal used to look after the property of Syed Ali Mollah and himself took the Job for recording the property in S.A. record in the name of Syed Ali Mollah and he reported that record was made in the name of Syed Ali Mollah. Syed Ali Mollah remained content with said report of recording. It is also stated that Syed Ali Mollah was a half mad, short in sight and hearing. Syed Ali Mollah died leaving plaintiffs Nos.1-4 as sons, plaintiff No.5 widow and two daughters, plaintiffs Nos.6 and 7 who all became owners in possession of the property and are paying rents and in the meantime, the R.S. survey commenced. The property in schedule 'Kha' out of Ka schedule property was recorded in their names. The plaintiffs were possessing 'Kha' schedule property on payment of rents peacefully without any obstruction. The defendants suddenly I claimed right and title in 'Kha' schedule property. Then, the plaintiffs on obtaining a certified copy of the B.S. khatian on 08.05.1983 from collectorate came to know about the erroneous recording. The recording of 'Kha' schedule property out of schedule 'Ka' property in the name of defendants was illegal. Ibrahim Mondal got it recorded in S.A. record in the name of Ibrahim Mondal instead of Ibrahim Mollah and in the names of his own daughters and wife. The defendants has no right; title and interest in the suit property. The claim of defendants in the suit property creating a cloud in the right and title of the plaintiffs and the suit was filed for removal of said cloud. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying the plaint Case stating that the suit was not maintainable in present form and was barred under the law of limitation. There was defect of parties. The Suit was not property valued. The defendants stated that the suit land under C.S. khatians Nos. 1537, 1538 and 1550 were originally owned by Manjony Bewa, who failed to pay rents, and consequently the property was sold in auction, and one Ibrahim Mondal purchased it in auction sale and on getting possession of the property owned the property peacefully; Ibrahim Mondal paid rents for 10.34 acres of land at fixed Jama at Tk.33.00 to the Raja Birendra Nath Roy Bhadur Estate, Natore in his name and paid rents. He was also locally known as chute Ibrahim Mondal. He subsequently transferred property measuring 10.34, by registered deed of Heba dated 12.10.1946 to his wife Sabiran Bibi alias Sabran Bibi, and daughter Rokeya Khatun. The wife and daughters owned and possessed the entire property. Rokeya by a deed of Heba dated 11.1.1958 transferred 330 acres of land to her husband Abdul Khaleque Khan, who in his turn enjoyed the property on payment of rents in his name. It was mentioned that Sabiran Bibi and Rokeya had inducted a Korfa tenant in 2.86 acres of and out of 10.34 acres of land and they had been possessing 7.48 acres of land as Rokeya made gift for 3.30 acres there remained 4.18 acres of land to them. Thus Abdul Khaleque, Sabiran and Rokeya possessed the land on payment of rents. By a sale deed dated 26.04.1967 Abdul Khaleque transferred his 3.30 decimals of land to his wife Rokeya, in lieu of her dower. Thus Sabiran and Rokeya begum possessed 7.48 acres of land. 

 4. Mr. T.H. Khan, Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the auction purchase of the suit land by the ex-Zaminder and getting delivery the possession of the same and the subsequent Pattan given to the Ibrahim Mondal, the predecessor of the defendants having been proved by evidence oral and documentary nothing remained with Manjony Bibi, either to make oral gift to Sayed all Mollah or getting the suit lands by inheritance by Sayed Ali Mollah from Manjony Bewa and also getting the suit land by inheritance by this plaintiffs, consequently,   said Sayed Ali Mollah and in his absence the plaintiffs did not bother to got the name of Syed Ali Mollah recorded in the S.A. Khatian and subsequently in the R.S. Khatian, finally published and having a presumptive value and the Appellate Court rightly allowed the appeal and dismissed the plaintiffs suit on proper analysis of a evidence and materials on record but the High Court Division totally avoided to consider the said vital points involved in the matter and most illegally and arbitrarily passed the impugned judgment not sustainable in law and is liable to be set aside. That as there is no scrap of paper of the plaintiffs to show documentary evidence of possession and P.W.s are all interested could not prove plaintiffs alleged possession of the suit lands in any manner whatsoever with wherein unspecified and vague statement of D.W. 3, which did not help in any manner, relating to the plaintiffs alleged possession far less specific possession and hence the appellate Court was quite justified in holding that the plaintiffs were not entitled to a decree for want of proper identification of the suit land i.e. 'kha' Schedule lands consisting in 16 different C.S. Plots at different places corresponding of 14 R.S. Plots but the High Court Division without recording any independent finding and on mere surmises and conjectures most illegally concurred with the finding of the trial relating to the plaintiffs alleged possession and passed the impugned judgment and thus committed a grave error of law. That the plaintiffs main Case of verbal gift not having been proved as observed by the High Court Division but on the alleged case of getting the property by inheritance as held by the High Court Division is not in the plaint and was not found by the Trial Court and the said Case not having been proved by any sort of evidence, the High Court was totally wrong in holding that the plaintiffs got the property in suit by inheritance and thus the High Court. Division committed error of law in making the Rule absolute; that the High Court Division committed error in law in passing the impugned judgment without recording any independent findings regarding the judgment of the trial Court; that the materials on record show that the predecessor of the defendants and after his death the defendants as well had been and have been in actual physical possession of the suit land asserting hostile title, enjoyed the usufructs of the suit lands and paid rent of the suit land from 1339-1400 B.S. and neither the plaintiffs predecessor nor the plaintiffs took any step for establishment of their title and recovery of possession of the suit lands within the statutory period of limitation and hence the plaintiffs suit is barred by limitation and they are not entitled to a decree for simple declaration of their title of the suit land and therefore, the suit of the plaintiff is also barred under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act also but the High Court Division totally ignored to record any findings on the said vital points of law and committed errors of law and passed the impugned judgment causing serious miscarriage of justices; that identifications and the manner of possession of 16 C.S. Plots not having been given specifically in the plaint as held by the Appellate Court, the plaintiffs are not entitled to a decree for simple declaration on vague description of the suit land but the High Court Division was wrong in holding that the suit properties has been identified describing the record of settlement of survey and the property was sufficiently identified as per order 7 Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the opposite parties, as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 49 of 2009 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Muktagacha, Mymensingh against the petitioners and one Ramjan Ali Khan, as defendant, for a decree of permanent injunction, stating that the property under SA Khatian No. 200 and RS Khatian No. 412 measuring 1.20 sataks belong to Md Hatem Ali and Ahmed Ali. BRS Khatian stand recorded in their names as per their share. Hatem Ali is owner of 80 sataks and Ahmed Ali is owner of 40 sataks. While they were in possession of the property amicably by partition, Hatem Ali by a sale deed No. 3249 dated 1-4-1997 transferred 10 sataks land and by another Deed No. 9623 dated 7-1-1998 transferred 22 sataks, totaling 32 sataks to the plaintiffs and delivered possession to them on the northern side of the plot. 

 3. The plaintiff after purchase filled up the low land constructed house thereon, started business in the premises by plaintiff Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 5 and let out some portion to Shadat Hossain, Ayen Ali, Akkas Ali and Liakat Ali on monthly rents and planted various type of trees in the vacant land. While the plaintiff went to mutate their names in the khatian, they found that in the two purchase deeds the plot number and khatian number wrongly written. Thereafter, they propose their vendor for correction of the deed, accordingly, Hatem Ali by two registered declaration No. 3744 and 3745 both dated 13-9-2006 rectified the error by substituting BRS Khatian No. 412 and plot 2565 in place of BRS Khatian No. 172 and Plot No. 2562. Thereafter, said Ahmed Ali from his 40 sataks share transferred 13 sataks, of land to one Shafiar by registered deed No 6244 dated 09-8-2000 and 16.25 sataks to defendant No. 4 Abu Bakker Siddique by deed No. 6243 and by a deed No. 6245 transferred 7.25 sataks to Shahera totalling 36.75 sataks. After transfer there remains only 3.25 sataks land and said Ahmed Ali by a registered deed No. 9025 dated 18-12-2005 transferred 4 sataks of land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in excess of his share but delivered possession in 3.25 sataks in place of 4 sataks. 

 10. He finally submits that for getting a decree of permanent injunction there must be a breach of an obligation existed in favour of the plaintiffs, expressly or by implication and the plaintiffs are to prove that the defendants invades or threatens to invades the plaintiffs right to or an enjoyment of property, but in the present case the plaintiff utterly failed to prove that the defendants threatened the plaintiffs right to or enjoyment of the property by any evidence, therefore, the trial court rightly dismissed the suit, it is also argued that but the appellate court while allowing the appeal failed to appreciate the fact that the plaintiffs utterly failed to prove cause of action for filing of the suit by any evidence as none of the PWs either in the examination-in-chief or in cross examination stated a single word alleging that the defendants threatened the plaintiff with dispossession on any date in their presence and the appellate court also failed to find that the defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit property and he never threatened the plaintiff with dispossession, as such, the judgment of the appellate court is liable to be set-aside. 

 15. From plaint and written statement this Court finds no dispute regarding title of vendors of the plaintiffs and the defendants. SA Khatian No. 119 (Exhibit-Ka) contain plot Nos. 384, 385 and 386 measuring 2.94 acres owned by three groups equally. The defendants claim that their vendors Ahmed Ali and Hatem Ali were owner of 1.45½ sataks land out of three plots. 

 16. From perusal of BRS Khatian No. 412 containing only plot No. 2565, this Court finds an area of 1.20 sataks has been recorded in the name of Hatem Ali and Ahmed Ali. Admittedly, Hatem Ali is owner of 2/3rd of the property and Ahmed Ali is owner of 1/3rd of the property. As per BRS khatian Hatem Ali got 80 sataks and Ahmed Ali, the vendor of the defendant No. 1 got 40 sataks only. Both the parties to the proceedings did not raise any question about correctness of BRS khatian finally published in the names of Hatem Ali and Ahmed Ali. In the absence of any objection, considering correctness of the BRS khatian and the sale deeds of the plaintiffs and the defendants it is found that the plaintiffs purchased 32 sataks of land from Hatem Ali by two sale deeds (Exhibits-2Ka and 3) and the rectification deeds (Exhibits-4 and 5). The defendant in their written statement at page 7, paragraph 10(ka) clearly and unequivocally admitted correctness of purchase of the plaintiffs by two sale deeds from Hatem Ali, the relevant portion of which is quoted below: 

 17. From above statement, this Court finds that the plaintiffs are in possession of their purchased land measuring 32 sataks for more than 9/10 years. Purchase deeds of the plaintiffs are earlier than the purchase deed of the defendant No.1. As per BRS khatian, Ahmed Ali owned 40 sataks of land in the suit plot No. 2565 but said Ahmed Ali by a deed No. 9025 dated 18-12-2005 transferred 4 sataks of land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 instead of having title in 3.25 sataks after earlier transfers.

5. The pre-emptee-petitioner resisted the pre-emption application by filing written statement denying most of the allegations of the pre-emption application contending, inter-alia; that the case land originally belonged to Simad Miah, Thanda Miah, Sydur Haque and others; Samad Miah and Thanda Minh transferred their share to Ezahar Meah by registered patta dated 14-6-1940 and Sydul Haque also transferred his share to Ezahar Meah by registered patta dated 2-6-1934 and after the death of Ezahar Meah his son Kanchan Miah alias Motahar Mean inherited the entire land and accordingly, his name finally published in BS Khatian. Thereafter, Kanchan Miah transferred the case land to the pre-emptee-petitioner on 6-7-2005 by registered deed with the full knowledge of the pre-emptor and other co-sharers and after purchasing the property the pre-emptee-purchaser mutated his name by opening mutation Khatian No. 2645. The pre-emptee purchaser has many lands surrounding the case land and that he is not a stranger to the case land. It has been also stated that the pre-emptor-opposite party is not a co-sharer at all and, as such, the case is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptee-petitioner after placing the impugned order as well as the judgment of the Mal Court below submits that the impugned order is not at all a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch the Court of appeal below without adverting the findings of the trial Court below abruptly arrived at a finding that the trial Court below committed illegality in holding that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer to the case jote. Mr Moudud Ahmed further upon referring the evidence of OPWs submits that the pre-emptee purchaser himself was examined as OPW-1, who in his evidence categorically stated that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer to the case land and the pre-emptee purchaser is a co-sharer to the case jote and he has more land surrounding the case land but the Court of appeal below as last Court of fact without considering the evidence of OPWs and without adverting the material finding of the trial Court below most illegally set-aside the judgment of the trial Court below which resulted in the failure of justice. Finally, Mr Moudud Ahmed submits that as per mutation Khatian No.2962 the co-sharer ship of the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 has been ceased and since the pre-emptor lost his co-sharer ship by separating his joma through Mutation Case No.7396 of 2011 he cannot apply for pre-emption. 10. Drawing support of his submission, the learned Advocate has relied on a decision reported in 55 DLR 214. 

 11. Mr Syed Shahidur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1, on the other hand, supports the impugned judgment and order which was according to him just, correct and proper. Mr Shahidur Rahman in the course of his argument upon placing judgments of two Courts below, deposition of witnesses submits that the pre-emptor in his deposition as well as pre-emption application categorically stated that he become a co-sharer to the case land by inheritance and thus, the Court of appeal below committed no illegality in holding that the trial Court com-mitted wrong in arriving at a finding that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer to the case land. The learned Advocate further submits that PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 categorically stated in their respective testimony that the pre-emptor-purchaser is stranger to the case jote and the claim of the pre-emptee-opposite party that he is a co- sharer to the case jote is false and without any legal basis. Finally, Mr Shahid Rahman, relied on the decisions reported in 35 DLR (AD) 54 and 34 DLR 180, and submits that the findings of the Court of appeal below are well founded in law and facts that the pre-emptor-opposite party No. I is a co-sharer to the case jote and he is entitled to pre-empt the land, is well founded in law and fact and the same should not be disturbed. 

 19. On going through the pre-emption application and written objection, it appears that the case land originally belonged to Samad Miah, Thanda Miah, Sydur Haque and others; Samad Miah and Thanda Miah transferred their share to Ezahar Meah by registered patta dated 14-6-1940 and Sydul Haque also transferred his share to Ezahar Meah by registered patta dated 2-6-1934 and after the death of Ezahar Meah his son Kanchan Miah alias Motahar Meah inherited the entire land and accordingly, his name finally published in B.S. Khatian, who sold out the case land to the pre-emptee-petitioner on 6-7-2005 by registered deeds and father of the pre-emptor named Alhaj Mvi. Md Harun Islamabadi purchased the land from the brother of Motahar (brother of Kanchan Miah) from the case holding by registered deeds dated 9-10-1997, 19-6-1997, 21-1-1998, 5-8-1997 and 13-4-1997 and in this way the father of the pre-emptor became co-sharer to the case holding in the year 1997 and the pre-emptee purchaser became co-sharer to the case holding in the year 2005. It further appears that both the parties after purchasing the land from parent joma mutated their names.

3. Defendant Nos. 8 and 9, 11-15 opposed the application for injunction contending, inter anti, that the plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit land. It has been further contended in the written objection that defendant Nos. 9-15 have title and possession over 3 decimals of land in suit plot No. 86 in which their homestead stands and the said land has also been duly recorded in their names in the RS Khatian and they have been paying rent regularly to the appropriate authority. It has been further contended that defendant No. 9 has already constructed a pucca building in suit plot No. 86 and there are other structures standing thereon and the said land is well fenced by walls on all four sides and under such circumstances there is absolutely no ground for granting temporary injunction on vague and indefinite assertions of the plaintiffs. 

 4. The learned Subordinate Judge by the impugned order dated 17-7-94 found that the plaintiffs have failed to make out a prima facie case in support of their claim for temporary injunction. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the materials on record also found that there is nothing on record to prima facie prove that the plaintiffs have possession in suit plot No. 86. On the other hand, the constesting defendants have produced the certified copies of the finally published RS Khatian in which 26 decimals of land has been recorded in their names. From the DCR and the rent receipts produced by the contesting defendant if is found that they have been paying rent to the appropriate authority for the said land. RAJUK has already approved their plan for construction of buildings in the said land. It has been clearly asserted in the written objection that the construction of the building has already been finished. Suit plot No. 86 admittedly measures 32 decimals of land in which the contesting defendants appear to have possession over 20 decimals of land. The plaintiffs alleged claim of 10 decimals of land in this particular part is totally vague and indefinite. In such circumstances, the learned Subordinate Judge found that the plaintiffs have failed to make out a prima facie case for injunction. From the facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record we find that the learned Subordinate Judge was perfectly justified in refusing the plaintiffs'' prayer for temporary injunction. We find no illegality in the impugned order calling for our interference.

full_judgment: 10. The plaintiff, in view of a recital in the will, claims that Brajahari was indifferent and callous type of man and as such he was not appointed executor though he was the eldest son of Banga Chandra. It appears to me that the question whether Brojahari was indifferent or callous type of man or a normal man is not very much relevant for the purpose of arriving at a decision in this suit. The relevant question is whether Brojahari left the homestead of his father or used to reside on that homestead. The will executed on 3rd Chaitra, 1284 Maghi era which corresponds to 1924 A.D. There is no evidence to show in which year Banga Chandra died except the statement of D.W.1 as referred to earlier. Now, from exhibits 6 and 6(a) it appears that the property was recorded in R.S. Khatians in the names of three sons of Banga Chandra in equal shares and not in the names of the deity. These khatiana were finally published in the year 1930. The plaintiff did not claim that the khatians were wrong. That means these khatians remained unchallenged. In these khatinas 3/1rd shares has been recorded in the name of Brojahari and as such it cannot be said that Brojahari left the locality. The D.W.1 in his cross-examination said that the marriage ceremony of Brojahari was held in his father's house. P.W. 5 who is 75 years old stated that Brojahari was known to him and he used to reside in the suit homestead and also died there. This is exactly the case of the contesting defendant. It is definite case of the contesting defendent that his father used to reside in the suit homestead and died there. In view of R.S. khatians and the statements of the P.W.1 and P.W. 5 as mentioned above it is quite clear the Brojahari used to reside in the homestead plot of his father till his death. So, there is no truth in the claim of the plaintiff that Brojahari had no right to enjoy the proshadi in view of the condition laid down in the will because he did not reside in the homestead of Banga Chandra.

Mr. Md. Md. Yousuf Ali, D.A.G.with Ms. Israt Jahan, A.A.G with Ms. Kamrunnahar Lipi, A.A.G ……. For the appellants.
