full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Habibul Gani, J:- On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution this Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the failure/refusal of the respondent No.4 to start a mutation case/proceeding in the name of the petitioner in respect of 91 decimals of land -appertaining to R.S.: Khatian No.10, S.A. Khatian No.68, S.A. Plot No.62 and other 79 decimals of land appertaining to R.S. (P.R.R.) Khatian No.92, S.A. Khatian No.57, S.A. Plot Nos.65/66 (total 1.70 acres of land) of mouza Madandia under P.S. Kotwali (Faridpur Sadar), District Faridpur pursuant to a decree passed by the competent civil Court in favour of the petitioner should not he declared to be illegal and is of no legal effect and why the respondent No.4 should not he directed to start a mutation case/proceeding in the name of the petitioner in respect of the land in question and/or to pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court seems fit and proper. 

 3. The short facts for disposal of the rule are that the father of the petitioner got ex-parte decree over the land in question in a case of specific performance of contract on 12.05.1975 in Title Suit No.50 of 1973 and subsequently, filed Execution Case No.10 of 1978 and got registered kabala through Court being No.5224 on 9.5.1978. After death of her lather she riled Title Suit No.88 of 2001 impleading her brothers and sisters as defendants for declaration that her father was mere a benamder in respect of the schedule property in question which was subsequently on compromise decreed in favour of the petitioner vide decree dated 16.08.2001. Thereafter, the petitioner on 16.09.2001 went to the office of the respondent No.4, Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kotwali (Faridpur Sadar) with an application for mutating her name but the Assistant Commissioner (Land) refused to receive the application saying that the land in question is a khash land and those have been leased out to other parties. The petitioner knowing about the land in question as khash land filed Title Suit No.164 of 2001 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur implcading the Government as defendants seeking declaration that the land in question is not a khash land and to declare the title over the land in question in favour of the petitioner wherein the Government and other defendants contested the suit by filing written statements. Learned Assistant Juke, Sadar, Faridpur after hearing decreed the suit on contest declaring the title of the suit band in favour of the petitioner vide judgment dated 07.07.2004. The Government preferred Title Appeal No.150 of 2004 against the said judgment dated 07.07.2004 before the learned District Judge. Faridpur which on transfer was heard by the learned Third Court of Joint District Judge, who vide its judgment dated 23.01.2007 was pleased to dismiss the appeal affirming title of the petitioner. The Government did not Pile any civil revision before the Hon’ble High Court Division challenging the decree of the Court of the appeal passed on 23.01.2007 in Title Appeal No.150 of 2007. Thereafter, the petitioner again went to the office of the respondent No.4. Assistant Commissioner Land, with an application for mutation of the schedule land in question but the office of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), was unwilling to receive the application rather abused her. It is further asserted that though the petitioner for a several times went to the office of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) for tiling mutation case but refused and on 05.01.2009 the petitioner again went to the office of the respondent No.4 for filing application for mutation of the schedule land but respondent No.4 Assistant Commissioner (Land) did not receive the said application rather abused her and drove her away from the office. Then the petitioner through registered post with acknowledgement due sent legal notice on 01.03.2009 requesting him to start a mutation proceeding by receiving the application for mutation through her lawyer but got no response. The petitioner finally went to the office of the respondent No.4, Assistant Commissioner Land on 15.03.2009 with an application for mutation and requested him to start a mutation proceeding but the Assistant Commissioner Land refused to receive the application for mutation and very furiously drove her away from his office. The _ petitioner again served a legal notice upon the respondent No.4 requesting him to start a mutation proceeding on 25.3.2009 but got no reply. Hence, the petitioner being failed to accept her application to the office of the respondent No.4, Assistant Commissioner (Land), Faridpur has been constrained to file this writ petition for a direction upon the respondent No.4 to receive the application for initiation of a mutation proceeding and to dispose of the same in accordance with law. 

 that after filing of the writ petition the petitioner received a reply of the legal notice dated 01.03.2009 from the respondent No.4 Assistant Commissioner (Land) vide Memo No.13-7/07-08-239 dated 01.04.2009 to which the respondent No.4 stated that the petitioner sought mutation from S.A. record but in the meantime latest i.e. present B.R.S. record of the concern Mouja has been finally published in the gazette and the land in question in the present Khatian has been recorded in the khash Khatian No.1 in the name of the Government. as such, there is no scope to mutate the land in the name of the petitioner. 

 5. The respondent No.1 Secretary. Ministry of Land by filing affidavit in opposition opposes the rule and denying material allegations made in the writ petition asserted that the land m question all along has been recorded in the khash khatian and the said land now also has been recorded as khash in the name of the Government in the khatian i.e. present B.R.S. Khatian in khash Khatian No. l. 

 6. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner vide solenama decree obtained title of the suit property and then went to the office of the respondent No.4, Assistant Commissioner (Land) for mutating her name. While office of the respondent No.4 was unwilling to receive the application for mutation from the petitioner informing tier that the property in question has been recorded in the khash khatian the petitioner filed Title Suit No.164 of 2001. against the Government for declaration of title and the learned Court passed decree in favour of the petitioner on contest vide judgment dated 07.07.2004. Learned Advocate again submits that the Government filed Title Appeal No.150 of 2004 before the learned District Judge but the same was dismissed on 23.01.2007. Learned Advocate further submits that the Government did not file any revisional application against the judgment of the Court of appeal and as such the title of the petitioner is still undisturbed. Learned Advocate again submits that the petitioner after obtaining the decree from the competent civil Court went to the office of the respondent No.4 for mutating her name but respondent No.4 Assistant Commissioner (Land) did not receive the application for mutation. Learned Advocate finally submits that the petitioner issued legal notice upon the respondent No.4 Assistant Commissioner (Land) through her lawyer and in reply to the legal notice the respondent No.4 stated that as the mutation sought on the basis of S.A. record there is no scope to mutate her name as because the present B.R.S. record has been finally published in the gazette in the name of the Government in khash khatian No. l. In this regard Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate contended that from the reply of respondent No.4 it is proved that the petitioner went to the office of the respondent No.4 who did not receive the application for starting mutation case and as such failed to perform his duty as Government servant in accordance with law. Mr. Bhuiyan further submits that it is the hounded duty of the respondent No.4 to receive the application and to start a mutation case and dispose of the same in accordance with law. 

 7. Mr. Biswojit Roy, the learned Deputy Attorney General by filing affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the respondent No. l. Secretary, Ministry of Land submits that the land in question has been recorded as khash land and it has been settled to the landless agriculturist families. He further submits that the schedule land is all along a khas land and the application for mutation could not be entertained as the mutation was sought from S.A. record while the schedule land has been recorded in the latest Khatian i.e. in the present B.R.S. record as khas on the basis of latest survey of the concern mouja and Government published final gazette notification of B.R.S. record showing the land in question as khash in khash Khatian No.) in the name of the Government. 

 8. Mr. Roy further submits that the petitioner had alternative efficacious remedy to the higher authority i.e. to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) (shortly ADC Revenue) and the petitioner could agitate her grievance to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) but not doing that the petitioner has come directly to this Court for invoking the extra-ordinary jurisdiction of this Court conferred under Article 102 of the Constitution which is not at all maintainable. Mr. Roy finally submits that there was no formal mutation proceeding before the respondent No.4 as such no order was passed by the respondent No.4 and in absence of any formal order the present application is totally misconceived. In support of his submission the learned DAG referred the case of Government of Bangladesh Vs. M. Anwar Hossain and others reported in 16 BLC (AD) 155. 

 10. It appears that the writ petitioner obtained contesting decree from competent civil Court in Title Suit No.164 of 2001 against the Government and the Government preferred Title Appeal k No.150 of 2004 against the said judgment. Admittedly, the appeal was dismissed on 23.01.2007 affirming the judgment of the learned Assistant Judge who decreed the suit in favour of the petitioner. The Deputy Attorney General on -query of the Court could not show any document that Government filed any revisional application against the judgment of dismissal of appeal by the Court of appeal. It further appears from annexure-H to the supplementary affidavit to the writ petition filed by the petitioner, the reply of the legal notice by the respondent No.4, that the respondent No.4 was reluctant to mutate the schedule land in the name of the petitioner on the ground that the mutation was sought from the S.A. record while the final survey of the land in question that is B.R.S. survey of the concern mouja has been finally published in the Government gazette in khash Khatian No.1 in the name of Government. By this reply it is clear to this Court that the petitioner truly .went to the office of ` the respondent No.4 with an application for mutation but the same was not received to initiate a mutation proceeding for disposal and as such the grievance of the petitioner sustain to the fact that the respondent No.4 did not receive the application for mutation and no formal order was passed by starting a, mutation proceeding. The contentions of the learned Deputy Attorney General that the petitioner could avail other remedy by filing application to the ADC (Revenue) and in absence of any formal order in the mutation proceeding the writ petition is not maintainable in the form of mandamus are not at all acceptable to this Court as the respondent No.4 being a Government officer while dealing with mutation of land of concern mouja was totally unwilling to receive the application for mutation and to dispose of the same by starting mutation proceeding in accordance with taw by passing an order. As the respondent No.4 did not do so and passed no formal order, the petitioner was deprived from taking next course of law meaning other efficacious remedy to the higher authority. 

 11. Chapter XVII of the State Acquisition and tenancy Act, 1950 in the heading of "Maintenance and Revision of the Record of Right" and Rule 23 of the Chapter VI of State Acquisition Rules, 1955 framed under the Act in the heading of "Maintenance of Record of Rights under Section 143 of the Act" are related to mutation process. Concern Assistant Commissioner land or other revenue officers, if empowered are duty bound to start a mutation proceeding either upon prayer of any person or as per procedure laid down in the aforementioned chapters and dispose of the same by passing necessary order after scrutinizing the previous records and documents and hearing the parties concerned. In the present case we find that the Assistant Commissioner (Land), respondent No.4 was unwilling to receive the application for mutation and failed to understand the legal proposition of aforementioned laws and rules and utterly failed to start mutation case upon receipt of the application for mutation from the petitioner. The respondent No.4 without starting mutation case by the reply of the legal notice informed the petitioner that as the mutation sought under S.A. record is not entertain able due to present B.R.S. record of the concern mouja has been published in the gazette notification showing the land in question as khash land in the name of the Government and gave no opportunity of hearing the petitioner. The Assistant Commissioner (Land) on receipt of the application could start a mutation proceeding and upon hearing the parties and scrutinizing the documents could pass any order in accordance with law and then the petitioner could take next recourse of law if aggrieved. It is apparent from the records and facts of the case that the petitioner repeatedly tried to file the mutation application to the office of the respondent No.4 and being failed, filed the present writ petition.

2. The respondent Nos. 1 to 6 herein, as plaintiffs, instituted Title Suit No. 68 of 1999 in the court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Dacope, Khulna against the government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna and others praying for declaration that the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 1/1998-99 by the defendant No. 4 declaring the suit land as government khas land is illegal, null and void, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs and also for permanent injunction. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that Rameshwar and others were the owners of 20.26 acres of land of SA Khatian No. 330 which was sold in Certificate Case No. 358/61-62 of the office of the Certificate Officer, Khulna and the plaintiff No. 1 auction purchased the 15 annas share of the said land and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 purchased 10 gondas share each in open auction held on 30-5-1962 and the sale was confirmed on 30-7-1962 and auction purchasers got sale certificate on 22-9-1962 and they got delivery of possession of the suit land through process of law and then mutated their names in the SA Khatian vide Mutation Case No. 9 of 1965 and they are in possession on payment of rent to the government. That the plaintiff No. 1 transferred some lands out of his auction purchased land to the plaintiff Nos. 2 to 6 and thus the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 6 are in possession of 18.99 acres of land. 

 3. That Kesta Majhee, son of Gour Gopal Majhee, instituted Title Suit No. 380 of 1963 in the court of the then 2nd Munsif, Khulna for setting aside the above auction sale which was ultimately dismissed on compromise. Thereafter Durlov Chandra Roy and others instituted Title Suit No. 259 of 1966 in the same very court against the plaintiff No. 1 and defendant Nos. 7 and 8 and others claiming right, title and interest in respect of 1.65 acres of land out of the above auction purchased land and obtained ex-parte decree on 14-2-1967. Challenging that decree the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 instituted Title Suit No. 314 of 1969 and obtained decree against which Durlov Chandra and others filed Title Appeal No.124 of 1973 which was ultimately dismissed after hearing. That Nilkanta Mandal-son of Madar Chandra Mandal also instituted Title Suit No. 770 of 1980 in the court of the then 1st Munsif, Khulna against the plaintiff No. 1, defendant Nos. 7 and 8 and others for declaration of their title in respect of 5.96 acres of land out of that auction purchased land which was ultimately dismissed on 7-1-1990. Thereafter Naren Majhee, son of Kesta Majhee, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 43 of 1990 before the defendant No. 3 against the plaintiff No. 1 and defendant Nos. 7 and 8 and others which was ultimately dismissed for default and then Naren Majhee instituted Title Suit No. 94 of 1996, which on transfer, was renumbered as Title Suit No.25 of 1998, for partition in respect of 4.6250 acres of land out of the auction purchased land but ultimately the said suit also was dismissed on 7-6-1998 for-non prosecution. That the defendant No. 2 by order dated 25-8-1996 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 1996, made the entire auction purchased land as Government khas land and as against that order the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 filed Appeal No. 334 of 1996 before the Additional Divisional Commissioner (Revenue), Khulna Division who allowed that appeal and directed the defendant No. 2 to dispose of the matter according to law and also directed the parties to maintain status quo in respect of the auction purchased land. The defendant No. 2 by order dated 25-8-1996, again made the entire auction purchased land as government khas land. As against that order several appeals were filed and ultimately in Appeal No. 27 of 1997-98, Land Appeal Board, after hearing, by order dated 28-8-1997 sent the case back on remand to the defendant No. 2 who in turn sent the same to the defendant No. 4 with direction to dispose of the case upon starting a miscellaneous case. The defendant No. 4 then, without any notice to the plaintiff No. 1 and defendant Nos. 7 and 8, started Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99 under section 92 (2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and by order dated 1-4-1999 made 15.6350 acres of land of SA Khatian No. 330 as government khas land leaving 4.6250 acres of land in favour of Naren Majhee. The plaintiffs alleged that the initiation of the proceeding of Miscellaneous case No. 1/1988-89 and all other subsequent actions were wholly illegal, void and of no legal effect and are not binding upon the plaintiffs. It is also alleged by the plaintiffs that they never abandoned their residence on the suit land and that they are in possession of the entire auction purchased land along with the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 and that the suit land cannot vest in the government as khas land. 

 5. The defendant No. 1 in its written statement stated that the suit property was found without any owner. That 37.00 acres of land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 98 of Mouza Sutar Khali under Police Station-Dacope belonged to Tarak Chandra Majhi, Gaur Chandra Majhi and Rakhal Majhi to the extent of 4 annas share each and to Shanyashi Mondol, Shibnath Mondal, Puma Charan Mondal, Haran Chandra Mondal and Ratikanta to the extent of 16 gondas shares each and the same was recorded in the RS Khatian No. 285 in the names of the descendants of those recorded owners including some of the aforesaid persons and that the said property was recorded in the finally published SA Khatian No. 330 in the name of the Rameswar, Gour Chandra, Rakhal, Shannyashi, Puma Charan, Ratikanta and others and that one Jiban Krishna Majhee and others, one set of the recorded tenants got 16.74 acres of land separated and recorded in SA Khatian Nos. 330(1), 330(2) and 330(3) and the remaining 20.26 acres of land remained in the original SA Khatian No. 330 in the names of Rameswar and others; that the recorded tenant Gaur Chandra Majhee while owning and possessing 4.6250 acres of land, died leaving behind his only son Kesto Majhee who has been possessing his property inherited from his father and that 15.63 acres of land is ownerless which was made government khas land in terms of report of the tahsildar under section 92(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act on 6-9-1994 against which appeal was filed and ultimately the matter was sent to the Additional Deputy Commissioner for final disposal and accordingly the Additional Deputy Commissioner sent the matter to the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Dacope who started Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99 under section 92(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and served notice upon both the parties and by order dated 1-4-1999 made 15.63 acres of land as government khas land and granted lease of the said property to the lessees in the year 1405 BS in Miscellaneous Case No. 37/98-99, 38/98-99, 31/98-99, 32/98-99 and 40/98-99 and that the lesees are in possession of the suit land within the knowledge of the plaintiffs. That the added defendant Nos. 9 to 19, the lesees are in actual possession of the suit land and that the story of auction purchase of the case land by the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 is false and baseless. 

 9. The High Court Division found that the contesting defendants could not produce any evidence or material before court to prove that the auction sale of the suit land in Certificate Case No. 358 of 1961-62 was fraudulent, collusive etc. The High Court Division observed that the original copy of the sale certificate-the Exhibit-4 was granted under the signature of the Certificate Officer, Chalna, Khulna on 27-9-1962 and that this Exhibit-4 proved that the suit land was sold in auction in Certificate Case No. 358 of 1961-62 and that this Exhibit-4 showed also that the possession of the auction sold land was delivered to the auction purchasers on 5-10-1962 by one Dhirendra Nath, a process server of the RCO Office, Chalna. The High Court Division pointed out also that after auction purchase the plaintiffs mutated their auction purchased land in their names in SA Khatian in Mutation Case No. 9 of 1965 and also paid rent regularly and were granted rent receipts. The High Court Division made observation to the effect also that the suit land could not be treated as escheat property on the face of Exhibit-3 the mutated khatian of the suit land in the name of the plaintiffs and that the government also could not produce any iota of evidence to prove the suit land became escheat property. The High Court Division took into consideration the previous suits (as mentioned by the plaintiffs in their plaint) filed by different persons in respect of the suit land against the plaintiffs and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 and noted that all those suits were ultimately dismissed by competent courts of law. The High Court Division pointed out also that the Government though filed written statement in this suit on 24-3-2000 but did not take any step to set aside the auction sale as yet. The High Court Division made observation to the effect also that in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99 the suit and though was declared as government khas land under section 92 (1) (a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, but there was nothing to show that any of the owners of the suit land died intestate leaving no heir rendering the suit land as escheat property. The High Court Division further found that before declaring the suit land as the khas land of the government treating the same as escheat property no notice was served upon the plaintiffs as per provision of law. The High Court Division made observation to the effect also that there was no evidence at all to prove that after declaring the suit land as khas land of the government as per section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the government took possession of the suit land. The High Court Division opined that the alleged 'eksona' lease of the suit land in favour of the defendant Nos. 9 to 19 and also few others is illegal and without jurisdiction and the government is now under legal obligation to restore possession of the suit land from its lessess to the SA recorded owners, the plaintiffs. 

 10. Being aggrieved by this judgment and order of the High Court Division the contesting defendants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1342 of 2006 before this Division and leave was granted to consider the submissions of the learned Counsel for the leave-petitioners to the effect that both the trial court as well as the appellate court below, upon proper consideration of evidence on record, dismissed the suit and there is nothing on record to show that the findings of the courts below are shockingly perverse or are vitiated by non-reading of the material evidence or misconstruction of any important documents affecting the merit of the suit and that the High Court Division upon mere surmise and conjecture held that since the lessees are in unauthorized possession the government is under legal obligation to restore possession of the suit land to the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 6 after evicting the lessees therefrom; that the High Court Division committed error of law in holding that no notice was served upon the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 under the provision of section 92 (3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99 overlooking the Exhibit-ঞ, the record of the proceeding of said Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99 and that the High Court Division, without controverting the findings of the courts below to the effect that notice of the said Miscellaneous case was duly served upon the plaintiff No. 1 and that there is no evidence to prove that the co-sharers of SA Khatian No. 330 resides in this country, erroneously held that the suit land was illegally declared as government khas land under section 92 (2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in Miscellaneous Case No 1 of 1998-99. 

 13. Mr Qumrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondents, on the other hand, has made submission to the effect that the original copy of the sale certificate, the Exhibit-4, proves that the suit land was sold in auction in the year 1962 and the possession of this land also was delivered in favour of the auction purchasers, that the contesting defendants though has claimed that this auction sale of the suit land in Certificate Case No. 358 of 1961-62 is collusive, fraudulent, but they could not produce any iota of evidence before court to substantiate this claim that the suit land was sold in auction by the government and the government mutated also the name of the auction purchasers in SA Khatian of the suit land and also received rents from the auction purchasers and granted rent receipts in favour of them regularly upto 1981 and in the circumstances the government now cannot say that the suit land, being escheat property, has vested in the government under section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned Advocate has argued that in this suit the contesting defendants did not state anything as to who were owners of the suit land and which of the owners of the suit land died leaving no heir and as to how the suit land became escheat property; that the government did not say anything as to what happened and when did it happen which authorized the government to invoke the powers of section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 to declare the suit land as khas land of the government. The learned Advocate has argued that the government itself allowed the plaintiffs to purchase the suit land in auction in the year 1962 and thereafter mutated the name of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land in SA Khatian and accepted rent from the plaintiffs for the suit land for a long time since 1962 and also granted rent receipts to the plaintiffs and in the circumstances the government cannot say now that the suit land became escheat property and, as such, it was made khas land of the government rightly. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondents has argued that the High Court Division, on meticulous examination of the evidence and other materials on record and on consideration of all aspects rightly set-aside the findings and decision of the courts below and rightly decreed the suit in part. 

 15. Admittedly, the suit land originally belonged to Rameshwar and others and it was recorded in SA Khatian No. 330 in the name of said owners. The plaintiffs' case is that for arrears of rent the suit land was sold in auction in Certificate Case No. 358 of 1961-62 of the office of the Certificate Officer, Khulna and the plaintiff No. 1 purchased 15 annas share and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 purchased the remaining anna share of the suit land in open auction held on 30-5-1962 and this sale was confirmed on 30-7-1962. To prove this case the plaintiffs have filed the original copy of the sale certificate which has been marked as Exhibit-4. It appears that the High Court division, on examination of this sale certificate and on consideration of all other facts and circumstances held that there was no reason to doubt the genuineness of this Exhibit-4. The High Court Division, on examination of this Exhibit-4 found also that this Exhibit-4 includes papers showing delivery of possession also which showed that the auction purchasers were duly deliverer possession of their auction purchased land on 5-10-1962 by one process server of the RCO Office, Chalna named Dhirendra Nath. We have also examined this Exhibit-4 which is the original copy of sale certificate. There is no reason to doubt the genuineness of this Exhibit-4. The contesting defendants though have alleged that the auction sale of the suit land was collusive and fraudulent, but did not plead any case to the effect that there was actually no such certificate case at all and the suit land was never sold in auction or that the Exhibit-4 is forged and manufactured by the plaintiffs. The Government-defendant did not bring the relevant register of certificate cases to show that there was actually no such certificate case in respect of the suit land and the suit land was never sold in auction in any such certificate case. In this circumstance the High Court Division rightly accepted this Exhibit-4 as genuine one and rightly held that this Exhibit-4 proves that this suit land was sold in auction. On scrutiny of this Exhibit-4 we also find that this Exhibit-4 includes some papers which show that the auction purchasers were given delivery of possession of their auction purchased land by a process server of RCO office, the learned Counsel for the Government-appellant did not raise any question as to these papers of Exhibit-4 showing delivery of possession either before us or at the time of seeking leave to appeal, though in the impugned judgment these papers were given importance by the High Court Division. The contesting defendants though have alleged that this allege auction sale of the suit land was fraudulent and collusive but could not adduce any evidence or materials before court to substantiate this claim. Rather, it appears that after this auction sale the government duly mutated the name of the auction purchasers in SA Khatian of the suit land the Exhibit-3 by starting Mutation Case No. 9 of 1965 and also accepted rent from the auction purchasers for a long period and granted rent receipts to them. The High Court Division, on consideration of all these facts and circumstances and evidence on record rightly opined that the government now, by saying only that the auction sale was fraudulent, cannot be absolved from discharging their onus to prove by sufficient cogent evidence that the auction sale was not held at the instance of the government or that there was illegality or irregularity in the conduct of the auction sale and that it was not a proper transaction. The High Court Division, upon consideration of the entire evidence and also pleadings of the parties, rightly found that no attempt at all was made from the side of the government-defendant to prove that the auction sale of the suit property was fraudulent one and was not initiated at the instance or the government as the certificate holder. The High Court Division rightly held also that according to section 20 of the public demand recovery act the auction purchaser's right, title and interest in the suit land became absolute from the date of auction held on 30-5-1962 and in the circumstance the suit property could not be treated as escheat property. 

 16. Evidently, the trial court and the appellate court below without examining and appreciating the Exhibit-4 properly and without taking into consideration the facts that the Government mutated the names of the auction purchasers in the SA Khatian of the suit land and also accepted rents from them and granted rent receipts to them came to the wrong findings and decision. The findings and decision of the courts of facts vitiated by misconstruction, misreading and non-consideration of material evidence and facts and circumstances on record. 

 17. In this suit the government though has claimed the suit property as escheat property but it appears that neither in their pleadings nor in the evidence has the contesting defendants made it clear at all as to how could the suit property be treated as escheat property. The contesting defendants have stated only that on a report of local tahshil office the defendant No. 4 declared the suit land as khas land of the government treating the same as escheat property in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99. But where in this suit it has been proved sufficiently that at the instance of the government the suit land was sold in auction in favour the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 in the year 1962 and the government also accepted this auction-purchasers as owners of the suit land by mutating their names in the SA Khatian of the suit land and also by accepting rents from them and granting rent receipts for a long period the treating of the suit land as escheat property by the government and there-by declaring the same as khas land of the government without making it clear in any manner as to how and why the suit property can be rebated as escheat property has been illegal. It should be mentioned here that before declaring the suit property as khas land of the government there were so many litigations in respect of the suit land. Several persons filed several suits against the auction purchaser’s plaintiff Nos. 1 and defendant Nos. 7 and 8 claiming the suit land but all those suits were ultimately dismissed. In this present suit the government-defendant, of course, has, contended that in none of those previous suits the government was made a party and, as such, the result of those suits are not binding upon the government. But the government, admittedly, could know about the auction sale in question in the year 2000 at least, when it filed written statement in this present suit but the government did not file any suit for declaring that auction sale of the suit land collusive, fraudulent etc as yet. It has been contended from the side of the contesting defendants that in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99 notices were duly served upon the plaintiffs. But in this present suit filed within the statutory period of limitation this question-whether notices of impugned Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99 were served upon the plaintiff or not is not at all important to be discussed and considered. The plaintiffs have right to challenge the impugned order passed in this Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99 before a civil suit within the statutory period of limitation even if they got notice of that miscellaneous case and appeared in that case and contested. 

 18. However, in this suit it has been proved sufficiently that the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 purchased the suit land in auction held at the instance of the government in the year 1962 and they also got delivery of possession of the suit land. The mutated khatian of the suit land in the name of the plaintiffs, series of rent receipts showing acceptance of the rents by the government from the plaintiffs for the suit land and also the oral evidence adduced by the plaintiffs prove sufficiently that the plaintiffs got possession of the suit land after their auction purchase and were also in possession of the same, at least till the suit land was leased out to different lessees by the government on the basis of the impugned order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1998-99. The plaintiffs have filed this suit in the year 1999. In the circumstances the High Court Division rightly directed the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1 to 4 to restore possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs upon evicting the lessees therefrom without delay making observation to the effect that the government granted 'eksona' lease of the suit land to the defendant Nos. 9 to 19 and few others illegally and without jurisdiction and, as such, the government is under legal obligation to restore possession of the suit land from its lessees to the SA recorded owners, the plaintiffs.

full_judgment:
2. The plaint case, in short, is that "Ka" schedule land was originally belonged to Sree Laksmi Narayan Thakur who got permanent settlement and while in possession; his name was finally published in CS khatian. Thereafter, he transferred the suit land to M/s Rally Brothers famous Jute Company under which hundreds of day labourers were working for carrying jute from the jute dealers bepary) boat to the mill. Day laborers used to get their remuneration from the beparies. For staying the day laborers, in 1324 BS on the land of Rally Brothers some temporary huts were constructed with bamboo and tiles. Rally Brothers did not take any rents from the laborers and also the laborers did not pay any rents to the Rally Brothers for staying in the temporary huts. In the cyclone of 1326 BS the temporary huts were totally blown away and in 1328BS the day laborers, despite obstruction raised by Rally Brothers, erected some kacha structures for their living. Rally Brothers tried to evict them but fail. In this way, the predecessors of the plaintiffs acquired title by adverse possession. On 17-9-1996 defendant No.6 invite tender in Daily Janakantha for selling 'ka' schedule land to the highest bidder. This tendered as not noticed by the plaintiffs. Defendant No.5 and others participated in the tender and defendant No.6 accepted the tender of defendant No.5. Defendant No.5 after purchase of 'ka' schedule land as aforesaid, now tried to dispossess the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs are in possession on the suit land for more than 70 years and acquired title by adverse possession, as such, defendant No.6 has no authority to sell the suit land. It has been prayed in the suit that:- 

 4. The case of defendant No.4 is that the suit land was originally belonged to Rally Brothers' in whose name the SA khatian and RS khatian No. 290 were prepared and was finally published. The plaintiffs, 71 in numbers, most of them are false and imaginary and failed to mention how the predecessors of them was living in the suit land specifically in the plaint nor they described in the plaint as to whose heirs are they. It is admitted fact that the suit land belonged to Rally Brothers' and Rally Brothers proposed to sell the suit land to the Government on 23-2-1977 and there was an agreement for sell and thereafter the possession of the suit land was delivered to Government of Bangladesh and Government of Bangladesh filed the suit praying for decree against the Rally Brothers and suit was decreed and pursuant to the decree Government of Bangladesh through Court got possession and become the absolute owner/holder of the suit property. Government of Bangladesh after selling the suit land to defendant No.5, delivered possession of the suit land and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 11. Mr Probir Halder, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants of Appeal No. 203 of 1999, submits that, the plaintiffs having been proved that they are in the suit land from 1326 BS, the Rally Brothers tried to dispossess the plaintiffs but failed to dispossess the plaintiffs, as such the possession of the plaintiffs against original owner of the suit property running notoriously adversely and hastily thereby the plaintiffs acquired a good title against the original owner, Rally Brothers, by adverse possession, as such, the learned Judge committed illegality in not decreeing the suit. Learned Advocate further submits that, plaintiffs being poor illiterate, as such, they have no knowledge of the auction purchase pursuant to the notification dated 17-9-1996 published in The Daily Janakantha and by this purchase, defendant No.5 acquired no title over the suit land. The learned Advocate further submits that, the plaintiffs being in possession, the suit property ought to have been hand over to the plaintiffs and the learned Judge having found possession of the plaintiffs against the original owner Rally Brothers running more than statutory period of limitation committed no illegality in directing for selling the suit property to the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate submits that on the fact of the given case this portion of the judgment should not be set-aside. 

 14. Although learned Judge' dismissed the claimed of the plaintiffs as to acquire of title by adverse possession but since the learned Judge directed the Government to sell the property to the plaintiffs as the plaintiffs are in possession, as such, the possession of the plaintiffs is to be considered first. It is the case of the plaintiffs that their predecessors went into possession at first on permission from Rally Brothers. Thereafter, a storm blown away their cutcha strictures and they by their own money again constructed shed/hut for their living on the suit land. From the own averments of the plaintiffs it appears that excepting permissive possession, there is nothing in their favour to hold that their possession is of their own. A person may be in possession for more than statutory period of limitation but if it is permissive possession none accrued any title excepting his possession under the original owner and, as such, permissive possession in no way give any benefit and such possession of a person is in fact actual possession of the owner of the suit land in which he is in possession. The land lord has every right to thrown him out of possession any time either with or without notice. Moreover, we find that none of the khatian prepared in the name of plaintiffs. CS porch was prepared in the name of Rally Brothers. It is their case that they has become more dangerous to the plaintiffs when it is found are not in employment of the Rally Brothers, but they were under the employment of "bepary' or merchant who brought Jute to Rally Brothers and the plaintiffs only carried the jute from the boat to the mill and they have been paid by the "bepari" that is boat men not by Rally Brothers, as such, they have acquired no right against the purchased not against the Rally Brothers. On a reference to the depositions of PWs 1,2, 3, 4 and 5 it appears that none of them could say from which date they are in possession of the suit land.

3. The petitioners case in short is that C S Plot Nos. 613, 614 and 616 and other plots were owned and possessed by Mahmud Ali and Amjad Ali having 8 annas share each. The names of tenants were recorded in CS khatian. The Plot Nos. 616, 613 and some portion of 614 were fallen in the Saham of Mahmud Ali who sold 30 decimals of land of Plot Nos. 613/614 to Aftabuddin Ostagar and Jamrat Bibi on 25-5-1939 but the scribe wrongly wrote Plot No. 616, though delivered possession in Plot Nos. 613 and 614. While Aftabuddin and Jamrat Bibi were in possession in Plot Nos 613 and 614 they sold out the same to Jamila Bibi on 24-12-1943 and thereafter Jamila Bibi sold 30 decimals of land to Sk Yousuf Ali on 29-4-1946 who sold the same to Kadam Ali on 13-9-1955. The SA Khatian was prepared in his name and thereafter Kadam Ali sold 9 decimals to the father of the petitioners on 12-7-1962 who mutated his name and paid rents and taxes to the Government. The father of the petitioners filed Title Suit No. 251 of 1976 for correction of Plot No. 616 and got decree on 21-4-1978. During 1979 one Abdul Malek disturbed peaceful possession of the father of the petitioners for which he filed Title Suit No. 476 of 1979 and got decree against that person. During RS record the case land was rightly recorded in the name of the father of the petitioners. Said Abdul Malek filed Title Suit No. 49 of 1983 & TS No. 86/90 against the father of the petitioners and those were dismissed. That father of the petitioners sold 4 decimals of land to the petitioner No. 1 on 11-5-1996 who his name and paid rent & taxes to the Government and got plan from RAJUK for construction of a 5-storied building and petitioner No. 1 as a officer of Agrani Bank got Loan to build 5 storied building and accordingly the petitioner No. 1 constructed a 5 storied building in the suit land. During Moha Nagori Survey and Settlement an area of 4 decimal of land was recorded in the name of the petitioner No. 1, 5 decimals of land in the name of the father of the petitioners against which one Quiyum objection case and that was dismissed. The aggrieved party preferred appeal and that was dismissed by order dated 8-4-2001. The DP Khatian Nos 514 & 515 became final after completing all the stages of survey namely Khana Pun, Bujarat and attestation and after disposal of objection cases and appeals those were sent to the press for publication. 

 4. It is the further case of the petitioner that the further of the petitioners gifted his 5 decimals of land to the petitioner Nos. 2-4 vide registered Hiba-bill-ewaz deed on 7-7-1999. Soon after the RS Khatian was finally published, the petitioner No. 1 and the petitioners No. 2-4 separately mutated their names and paid rents and taxes to the Government. The petitioners have been possessing the suit land since 1962 by constructing pucca building and the Government is receiving rents and taxes regularly without any objection. The photo state true copies of the CS, SA, RS, SA Mutation Khatian, RS Mutation Khatian and DP Khatians and last Rent Receipts have been annexed and marked as Annexures- "A- 12 and A-13" respectively. The DP Khatians became final in the year 1999 and against that the objection case and Appeal under section 30 and 31 was also dismissed in the year 2001. The Respondent No. 5 Railway did not file any objection case against D P Khatian. The land as described in the Writ Petition is not the acquired land of the Railway authority did not take any steps against any actions of the petitioners since 1962. Rather the petitioners mutated their names constructed 5 storied building after taking "No objection certificate" from the Railway office did not raise objection against SA or RS settlement Record nor raised objection against recent survey but all on a sudden the petitioner No. 1 and the father of the petitioners got notices for Rehearing of the earlier Appeal No. 10121 of 2000 and hearing of new Appeal Nos. 77717/30 and 777725/30 filed by the Railway Estate Officer, Dhaka The petitioners appeared and submitted all the necessary papers. The Assistant Settlement Officer allowed the appeals of Railway by the impugned orders dated 4-9-2003 and 7-9-2003 which was counter signed by the settlement officer on 16-9-2003. The petitioners obtained the certified copy of the same. The certified copy of the orders of objection case and Appeal filed by Quiyum dated 11-4-2000 & 8-4-2001 and the notices dated 38-7-2003 have been annexed in the Writ Petition and marked as Annexures-"B, B-1, B-2, B-3 & B-4" 

 8. Mr Osman Gani, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that the land as described in the Writ Petition has been in possession of the petitioners and their predecessor since 1962 and the S A record, R S record were prepared in their names and they paid rent vide annexure-A series and B series. He further submitted that in against the recent survey held under the revisional settlement, some disputes were made against the DP Khatian and thereafter appeals were also preferred. He submitted that the petitioners being in possession since 1962, the Railway can not dispute the recording of the petitioners name and cannot prefer appeal under Rule 31. He further submitted that Rule submitted that Rule 42 and 42(A) are not applicable in the instant case. He prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

 11. We have considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates. Upon perusal of the Writ Petition as well as the statements made in the Affidavit-in-opposition, it is admitted that the petitioners are in possession, upon the land as described in the Writ Petition. Front the copy of the gazette notification which has been annexed as Annexure 1, it shows 1 that some property was acquired by Railway. From the copy of the said Gazette notification it is difficult to find out or detect that the land as described in the Writ Petition was acquired by the Railway. The alleged acquired land is unspecified. There is nothing on record to show that the Railway ever exercised its act of physical possession since 1960 upon the land as shown in the Writ Petition. It appears that the petitioner and their predecessors have been exercising their act of physical possession continuously since 1962 as the S A record and the R S records were prepared in their names and they are paying rent to the Government vide Annexure-B series. Annexure-A series are the Khatians. In view of the above facts and circumstances and unless it is shown specifying particular portion of land which was acquired by Railway, it is difficult to accept the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the respondents that the scope of enter-taming appeal under 31 of the Settlement Rules, 1955 was not open before the Railway to submit appeals. There is nothing available on record to show that any fraud was committed in getting recorded the names of petitioners in the DP khatian. As such, the application of Rule 42 and 42(A) are not available.

lawyer:
Fazlul Karim, Senior Advocate with N. K. Saha, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-On-Record ----- For the Appellants

full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff-appellants, in short, are that the suit property measuring .71 acres of land appertaining to three plots in C.S. Khatian Nos. 456 and 458 of Mouza Gopar, Police Station Keranigonj, District-Dhaka as morefully described in the schedule to the plaint was correctly recorded in the name of the Deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha and Hari Priya Baisnabi was its shebait and accordingly the impugned C.S. Khatians were prepared and finally published in the name of Deity. Hari Priya Baisnabi alias Dukhi Baisnabi as the Shebait of the deity constructed homestead in the suit land to perform the religious rites of the Bigraha. On the death of Hari Priya Baisnabi the religious minded persons requested the predecessors of the respondents Khapa Chan& Bairagi to perform the religious rites of the deity. Accordingly Khapa Chand Bairagi performed the religious rites of the Deity residing right in the suit property. The S.A. Khatian was prepared in the name of the defendant-appellant and finally published; that the local people were not aware about the wrong recording of S.A. Khatian. So they could not file any objection; that in 1970 the local people filed a Miscellaneous Case under Section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for correction of the S.A. Khatian in the Court of the Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka (now Assistant Judge) against Khepa Chand Bairagi which was subsequently dismissed for non-prosecution; that after the death of Khepa Chand Bairagi his two sons did not create any hindrance in the performance of the religious rites of the Deity that the local people came to know that the sons of Khepa Chand Bairagi are trying to dispose of the suit property and as such on 03.05.1985 local religious minded people formed a committee to run the religious rites of the Deity; that in 1987 one Kebel Chandra Sarker, General Secretary of the Committee filed a petition before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Keraniganj for correcting the S.A. Khatian in the name of the Deity and on that petition Mutation Case No. 1002/87-88 dated 28.10.1987 was started and the S.A. record was corrected by mutating the suit property in the name of the Deity. But the defendant-appellants raised an objection for cancellation of the said mutation case before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Keraniganj claiming their title in the suit property and that Mutation Case No. 1052/84-85 was restored; that subsequently all the mutation cases were disposed of in favour of the defendant-appellants. 

 4. The defendant-appellants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made by the plaintiffs-respondents contending, interalia, that the suit property measuring 35 decimals of land was recorded in the name of the Deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha as a rent receiver and one Hari Priya Baisnabi as its Shebait, possessed the same as rent free tenant and .35 acres of land in plot Nos. 151 and 153 under C.S. Khatian No. 458 was recorded in the name of Kunju Bihari. Mondal; that Hari Priya Baisnabi used to reside in the suit land; As she became old and was unable to move she brought Khepa Chand Bairagi to reside in the suit property who used to deal with harbal medicine and that in 1948 Hari Priya Bisnabi died and after her death her only heir Khepa Chand Bairagi inherited the suit property and possessed the same along with the members of his family running harbal medicine business there-in; that prior to that there was no Deity in the suit property and the C.S. recorded bargader also did not possess the same; that after whole sale acquisition the suit property vested in the Government and thereafter in 1951 Khepa Chand Bairagi took pattan of the suit land in his name correctly and possessed the same as his own property; that he never performed any religious rites of the Deity; that on 31.01.1977 Khepa Chand Bairagi transferred the suit property by deed of gift in favour of his two sons and wife-defendant-appellants and mutated their names vide Mutation Case No. 1052/84-85 dated 26.11.1984 and paid rent to the Government; that on 03.01.1990 these defendant-appellants came to know that their mutation case has been cancelled and the Khatian has been restored; that the plaintiff-respondents filed Review Case No. 76/90-91 against which the defendant-appellants filed Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 1992 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) and the mutation cases were restored; that the plaintiff-respondents preferred appeal which was disallowed on 04.04.1993; that the plaintiff-respondents in collusion with some local notorious persons forcibly dis-possessed the defendant-appellants from 5'X6' yards of land of the suit property and that they installed a Deity there but in fact in the suit property there was never any Deity; that the suit property is the paternal property of the defendant-appellants. 

 8. Mr. Fazlul Karim, Senior Advocate with Mr. N.K. Saha, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record appearing for the appellants submits that the High Court Division most illegally passed the impugned judgment and decree dismissing the appeal without considering that the suit is barred by limitation. He then submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division without any valid reason opined that the alleged registered deed of gift was not a valid deed of gift admitting that the defendant-appellants have been possessing the suit land as their own property for more than 12 years. He then submits that the S.A. Khatian and R.S. Khatian were recorded in the name of the appellant's father and Khepa Chand Bairagi by a registered deed of gift transferred the suit property on 13.01.1977 in favour of his widow and two sons. He finally submits that present appellants have been possessing the suit land on payment of rent to the Government Sheresta and as such the impugned judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 9. Mr. Herandra Nath Nandi, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-On-Record, appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that the suit property being a Debuttar Property and the appellants being not owners, Shebaits or next friend of the Deity have got no locustandi to contest the suit and prefer the appeal as they have no right, title and interest and possession in the suit land. He then submits that having regard to the facts that the C.S. Khatians were correctly prepared and published in the name of deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew I3igraha and Hari Priya Baisnabi as the Shebait and the said property belonged to Niskar Brahmmatra and completely dedicated to the plaintiff deity; that wrong recording of S.A. Khatian and R.S. Khatian in the name of the defendant-appellants should not cover any title to the suit property upon them and admittedly the defendant-appellant failed to show any papers showing that the suit property was vested in Government and the Government gave pattan to Khepa Chand Bairagi. He then submits that the High Court Division as a Court of Appeal rightly found that once the Debuttar Property is vested to the alter of Deity it cannot be divested and the suit property in the present case was rightly recorded and dedicated in the name of Deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha. Mr. Nandi, the learned Advocate for the respondent finally submits that the 'Ka' schedule property is Debuttar Property as Vested upon the Deity and transfer of the said property by the alleged registered deed in favour of the appellants are collusive, illegal and null and void and as such the question of limitation does not arise and the suit was filed very much within the period of limitation. 

 10. From the careful perusal of the impugned judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division it appears that the High Court Division found that C.S. Khatian No. 456 was rightly recorded in the name of Hari Priya Baisnabi as Shebait and the Deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha was the raiyat. So we cannot agree that the plaintiff Deity had rent receiving interest in the suit property. The High Court Division also rightly found that the suit land of C.S. Khatian No.458 comprising plot Nos. 151 and 153 has been recorded as Brahmatra under C.S. Khatian No. 456 and as a Shebait Hari Priya Baisnabi was in possession. It also appears that the High Court Division also found that there is no people showing that Khepa Chand Bairagi took jot pattan of the suit property in the year of 1951 but there is no paper that the property was vested in the Government and the Government gave pattan to Khepa Chand Bairagi. Once the suit property is vested in the Deity it cannot be divested and the Debutter Property under Section 415 of the Hindu Law is inalienable. The Shebait can reside for the purpose of performing religious rites and for the benefit and preservation for the Debutter Property. The learned Judge of the High Court Division rightly found that the deed of gift created by Khepa Chand Bairagi in favour of the defendants is void ability. It is well established by the Supreme Court that as a general rule of Hindu Law property given for the maintenance of religious worship is inalienable. In the case of Hunooman Persaud Vs. Mst. Babooee reported in 1856-6-MIA 393 it has been held that Shebayet has no power to alienate the Debater Property except in a case of need or for the benefit of the estate. He is not entitled to sell the property for investing the price of it to bring in an income larger than that derived from the property itself. 

 15. In the instant case admittedly the suit property was recorded in the C.S. Khatian as Debutter Property in the name of Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha and Hari Priya Baisnabi. After the death of Hari Priya Baisnabi, Khepa Chand Bairagi was inducted in the suit property as Shebait and residing for the purpose of performing religious rites. Both the Courts below made concurrent findings that the defendant failed to show any document that the suit property was vested in the Government and then the Government gave pattan of the suit property in favour of Khepa Chand Bairagi in 1951. Rather it has been proved by the plaintiff-respondent that Khepa chand Bairagi was inducted in the suit property as shebait to perform religious rites of the Deity. A shebait does not acquire any title to the Debutter Property. The Debutter Property can not be alienated by him except in case of unavoidable necessity. There is no denying the fact that the shebait can reside in the suit property for the purpose for performing religious rites. It does not create any title in his favour so Khepa Chand Bairagi was not legally entitled to transfer the suit property by a deed of gift in favour Of the defendants-appellants: Accordingly both the Courts below rightly found that the said deed of gift is illegal and void abilities. We are of the view that mere recording of some ones name in the S.A. or R.S. Khatian does not create any title to the property. In the instant case the General Secretary of the Committee on behalf of the Deity has filed the suit in respect of the Debuttar Property which is very much supported by the decision of the Indian Supreme Court reported in AIR-1967(SC) 1044 and the decisions of this Appex Court reported in 39 DLR (AD) 42 and .51 DLR (AD)156.

The learned counsel for the pre-emptee petitioner submits that the High Court Division fell in error in not considering that the deed dated 27.7.87, against which pre-emption is sought, is not in fact a transfer deed as in the same value of the case land was shown at merely Tk. 98/- and further the possession of the land covered under the above deed was also not delivered and so the above deed may be termed as a deed for protection of possession of the pre-emptee petitioner against which a pre-emption case is not maintainbale; the appellate Court correctly found that the pre-emptee is not wholly a stranger in view of the fact that her husband Ranju Miah was one of the co-sharers in the R.S. Khatian No. 2480 and further as the B.S. Record was not correctly prepared and for that the recorded tenant executed and registered the above deed dated 27.7.87 for removal of that mistake and the said deed as is in fact not a sale deed; the High Court Division having had failed to take notice that the pre-emptee petitioner was not a stranger to the case jote and that she has been possessing the case land and residing in the homestead situated therein for long time and if the pre-emption case is allowed the paternal homestead of the petitioner will go into the hand of the pre-emptor. 

 6. As it appears the High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding that the pre-emptor purchased a portion of the case jote by Ext. 5(Ka) and his name was recorded in the B.S. record, Ext.3, in Khatian No. 54 and the rent receipts Ext.4 series, also show that he, after purchasing the said land, mutated his name and paid rents regularly and he, as co-sharer, is in possession in the case land and the B.S. Khatian which has been published finally does not contain the name of the pre-emptee and the pre-emptee has also not challenged that preparation of B.S. Khatian in the name of the pre-emptor and so prima facie the pre-emptor appears to be a co-sharer and further the title of the pre-emptor in the case land can be challenged by the pre-emptee only in a properly constituted title suit.
