-Vs-
Kulsum Bibi and others ---------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal are that the present respondents as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No.65 of 1991 in the 1st Court of Senior Assistant judge, Rajshahi, impleading the present petitioners as defendants for partition of the suit land contending interalia that the suit land measuring .57 acres of land under S.A. Khatian No.178 belonged to Kasimuddin and Samir Mondal in equal share obtained through pattan; Their names were accordingly finally published in S.A. Khatian; The Plaintiff no.1 is the daughter of Kasimuddinis first wife; After the expiry or plaintiff no. l's mother said Kasimuddin again married defendant. Meher Nigar and out of that wedlock plaintiff no.2 was born; While possessing half of the suit land, said Kasimuddin died leaving daughters, widow Meher. Nigar and nephew Abdul Kader as his legal heirs; On the other hand, 3,l mir Mondal while possessing the rest half of the suit land died leaving defendant nos.2 and 3 as his heirs; After the death of Kasimuddin said Meher Nigar received her share from other lands and sold the same to Chandicharan Sarker and ethers; Said Abdul Kader sold his share received from Kasimuddin to Professor Mozaharul, Islam and others; The plaintiffs while enjoying half of the suit land with defendant nos.1-3 in ejmali gave authority to defendant no.1 for recording R.S. Khatian; After getting final record of the R.S. Khatian the plain-tiffs for the first time came to know that it was wrongly recorded in the name of defendants alone and hence constrained to file the suit for partition since there is no earlier partition by metes and bounds. 

 3. Defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending interalia that the suit land originally belonged to Damon Mondal who expired leaving behind son Samir Mondal and daughter Arjan Bibi as his heirs; Said Arjan Bibi gave up her share in favour of her brother; Said Samir Mondal died leaving minor son and daughter defendant nos.1 and 2 and widow defendant no.3 as his heirs; Since then defendants are owning and possessing the suit land; R.S. Khatian was correctly recorded in their names; Since S.A. Khatian was wrongly recorded half of the land in the name of Kaimuddin the plaintiffs taking that opportunity filed this false suit which is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. Plaintiffs in support of their case examined 4(four) witnesses and produced 4(four) rent receipts which are arked as exhibit-1 series, certified copy of S.A. Khatian no.178 marked as exhibit-2 and certified copy of C.S. Khatian no. 244 marked as exhibit-2.(Kha). On the other hand the defendants examined 5(five) witnesses and produced R.S. Khatian no.328 which is marked as exhibit-'Ka', S.A. Khatian no.178 and 2(two) rent' receipts marked as exhibit-'Kha', 'Kha(1)' and 'Kha(2)', death certificate of Kasimuddin marked as exhibit-'Ga' and certified copy of register relating to death of Kasimuddin marked as exhibit-'Gha' and 'Gha(1)', 2(two) photocopy of the letters sent by the Rajshahi Univerity to Samir Mondal which are marked as exhibit-'Uma' and `Uma(1)', certified copy of the sale deed sold by Meher Nigar which is marked as exhibit-'Cha'. 

 15. Above statement of cross examination by the P.W.I nullify the averments made in paragraph. no.2 of the plaint that the plaintiffs while enjoying half of the suit land with defendant nos.1-3 in ejmali gave authority to defendant no.1 for recording R.S. Khatian and after getting final record of the R.S. Khatian the plaintiffs for the first time came to know that it was wrongly recorded in the name of the defendants alone and thus constrained to file the suit. 

 16. It may he mentioned here that the PW.1 produced 4(four) rent receipts which are marked as exhibit-I series, certified copy of S.A. Khatian No.178, marked as exhibit-2 and certified copy of C.S. Khatian No.244 marked as exhibit 2 f(Kha)'. But the plaintiffs failed to prove pattani settlement in the name of their predecessor Kasimuddin by which they are claiming title in the suit land.

caseno: First Appeal No. 443 of 2012 with Civil Rule No. 988(F) of 2012
lawyer:
Mr. Quamrul Haque Siddique, Advocate with Mr. Ranjit K. Barmon, Advocate ......For the plaintiff-appellants
Mr. Mostafa Niaz Mahmood, Advocate with Mr. Md. Golam Noor, Advocate…..For the defendant-respondents.
parties:
Feroza Begum and others ……Plaintiff-Appellants
Vs.
Md. Nannu Mollah and others.....Defendant-Respondents.
full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, are that one Asan Ali was exclusive owner of 24 Decimals of land in Petty (C.S.) Khatian No. 163, plot No. 3620 , S.A. Khatian 1427 and 1642, plot No. 1062 area ˙23 decimal and plot No. 1062 area ˙01 decimal were finally recorded in the name of Ason Ali and others in respect of 1.53 decimal including ˙24 decimal; that while Ason Ali had been owing and possessing ˙24 decimal land of plot No.290/3620 and executed a Sale Deed No. 7534 dated 11.10.1963 and on the same day Yasin Matbor executed a registered agreement No. 7535; that is was stipulated in the agreement that Ason Ali will return Tk.800.00 within 8 years (within Magh 1370 BS- Poush 1378) in that case Yasin Matbor will execute reconveyance deed in favour of Ason Ali in respect of Suit ‘KA’ schedule; that thereafter Ason Ali transferred the said ˙24 decimal including other land to Rustom Ali, predecessors of the plaintiffs by registered Heba-bil-Ewaz Deed No. 668 dated 19.01.1965 but in the Heba Deed inadvertently Khatian No. 136 was recorded in place of Khatian No. 163, later on Ason Ali and Yasin Matbor died; that Yasin Matbor, before his death made Wasiatnama infavour of his First wife, Amirunnessa and son Fazal Haq declaring that if Rustom Ali son of Ason Ali return the loan money then they will return the mortgaged property; that plaintiff’s predecessor requested the wife and son of Yasin Matbor to execute reconveyance deed accordingly upon receiving Tk. 800/- from Rustom Ali, Amirunnessa herself and on behalf of her minor sons and daughter and Fazal Haq executed registered Saf Kabala deed No. 381 dated 08.01.1969; that B.S. Khatian and D.P. Khatian No. 4736 prepared in the name of Rustom Ali; that there after Rustom Ali died leaving behind the plaintiff nos. 1-10 as wife, son and daughter, who inherited suit the ‘KA’ schedule land and the plaintiffs having been in possession and enjoyment of the property mutated their names by opening separate Khatian No. 104113 and by paying all kinds of Khajna; that although the defendant nos. 1-4 heirs of late Yasin Matbor, have no right, title and interest in the suit schedule land but the defendant nos. 1-4 as vendors executed registered Sale Deed No. 1206 dated 09.02.2011 infavour of Nannu Meah, defendant no. 1 in respect of land described in schedule ‘KA’ to the plaint; that defendant no. 1 threatened the plaintiffs on 10.02.2011 that he will dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land; that the plaintiffs after obtaining certified of the said Sale Deed and being confirmed about the sale of the suit land, the plaintiff was constrained to filed the present suit for the reliefs stated above. 

 10.Mr. Quamrul Haque Siddique, learned Senior Advocate with Mr. Ranjit K. Barmon, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant submits that the heirs of Yasin Matbor paid Taka 800/- and they by kabala dated 08.01.1969 (Exhibit-9) re- conveyed the land to Md. Rustom Ali, son of Ason Ali Gazi. He further submits that the present contract for sale time is not essence of the contract but in contract for re- conveyance time is the essence of contract. He next submits that the trial court erroneously found that the heirs of Yasin Matbor was minor but infact the heirs of Yasin Matbor after attaining majority sold the land to Nannu Mollah, defendant no. 1 by kabala dated 09.02.2011 (Exhibit-2). He also submits that the heirs of Yasin Matbor returned the original sale deed (Exhibit-3) dated 11.10.1963 to the heirs of Ason Ali at the time of re- conveyance dated 08.01.1969 and delivered possession. Subsequently, suit land was recorded in the D.P. Khatian (Exhibit-5) and during pendency of the suit B.S. Khatian was finally published in the name of Rustom Ali and he paid rent regularly. He lastly submits that Ason Ali was alive in 1969 when the re-conveyance deed was executed by Yasin Matbor in favour of Rustom Ali. In support of his submission learned Advocate for the appellant cited a decision reported in 11 DLR 169. 

 12. He further submits that the plaintiff filed the suit for cancellation of Sale Deed No. 1206 (Exhibit-8) in the name of defendant No.1 executed by defendant Nos. 2-4. But defendant No. 1 also purchased the land of the suit khatian from the heirs of Yasin Matbor by sale deed No. 1367 dated 14.02.2011(Exhibit Kha). But in the suit plaintiff only prayed for cancellation of deed No. 1206 (Exhibit-8). Thus the suit is not maintainable due to partial claim for cancellation of deed no.1206 only. Learned Advocate next submits that the defendant No.1 after purchase of the suit land transfer his entire purchased land by 5 (five) registered kabalas being Exhibit-Ja(1) to Ja(5) in favour of Md. Humayun Kabir Chowdhury, Md. Abdul Baset Sarker, Md. Khorshed Alam Mollah, Md. Harun-or-Rashid and Mohammad Jahangir Alam, Mahbub Alam and Soheli Sultana respectively and the aforesaid purchasers are in possession of the suit land but the plaintiff did not implead them as party in the present suit. So, for by non-impleading of the aforesaid necessary parties, the present suit is bad for defect of parties. 

 15. Learned Advocate finally submits that Agreement for re-conveyance Deed No.7535 dated 11.10.1963 (Exhibit-3 (Ka) for a period of 8 (eight) years from Magh 1370 B.S to Poush, 1378 B.S which expired on 10.10.1971 and after that the transaction has become past and closed. Thus the plaintiffs cannot take advantage of President’s Order No. 88 of 1972. Since the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1951 was amended and section 95 has been incorporated by inserting by the President’s Order No. 136 of 1972 with effect from 03.08.1972. Since the transaction was not alive at the relevant time as such the plaintiff is not entitled to get relief. In this respect learned Advocate refers the decisions reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233 and 16 BLT (AD) 55.

lawyer:
Mr. M.G.H. Ruhullah, Advocate, For the petitioner. 
Mr. Dipayan Saha, A.A.G, For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Sree Kanailal Boshak
Vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Naogaon and another
full_judgment:
2. The facts giving rise to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted the original Other Class Suit No.66 of 1998 in the Court of learned the then Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Naogaon against the defendant-opposite party for declaration of title in respect of 'Ka' schedule property contending inter alia that the suit property appertaining to Mouza Hajinagar under Neyamatpur police station of District-Naogaon corresponding to C.S. khatian No.107 and S.A. khatian No.2, 88 and R.S. khatian No.1 in C.S. plot No.733, 212, 176 and present plot No.1145, 82 and 123 comprising an area of 3.60 acres of land originally belonged to Koibara Estate. The Zamindar of the said estate while owning and possessing the suit property transferred 0.18 acres of land out of 2.43 acres of C.S. plot No.733 in favour of one Krishna Mohon Fouzdar and the remaining portion of the 'Ka' schedule land was settled in favour of the plaintiff in the year 1351 B.S. at a 'Najar' of Tk.105/- (one hundred and five). The plaintiff paid rent to the Zamindar and obtained 'dakhila'. Subsequently, while the land vested upon the government the plaintiff paid rent to the government `seresta' and the S.A. 107/5 attested khatian was prepared in the name of plaintiff and thereafter, during R.S. operation the land has been correctly prepared in the name of the plaintiff in field `bujarat' khatian No.632. Subsequently, while the khatian was finally prepared in the name of defendant No.2 the plaintiff filed an Objection Case being No.195/1972, which was allowed on contest on 22.10.1972. The legal heirs of Krishna Mohon Fowjdar by a transfer deed dated 08.04.1997 sold out his 18 decimals of land of 'Ka' schedule in favour of the plaintiff and the sub-kabala was registered in Neyamatpur Sub-registry Office. In this way, the plaintiff after acquiring the entire 'Ka' schedule property use to possess the same and on 09.07.1998 the Union Land Office declined to accept rent from the plaintiff, disclosing that the property-in-dispute has become khash property under the government and the government will settle the land. Thereafter, on 19.08.1998 on getting the certified copy of the khatian, the plaintiff came to know that the suit property has been wrongly recorded in the name of government, which constrained the plaintiff to institute the original suit for declaration of title. 

 3. The contrary case of the government in short is thus, that the suit is not maintainable and barred by limitation and the same is bad for defect of parties. The further case of the government-opposite party is such that during R.S. operation the land has been correctly recorded in the name of government as khash land as the land is under the "Shyrat Mohol" and in the remark column of the khatian, it has been cited that the property is being used by the people of the locality at large from the very beginning, using the water of the suit property for their agricultural purposes and the plaintiff having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the suit property on the basis of false allegation filed the suit. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned Appellate Court during disposal of the appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned court of appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by not considering that the plaintiff obtained settlement of the suit land on 27th Magh of 1351 B.S. and the settlement paper has been properly proved by the plaintiff which has been marked as Exhibit-1. The subsequent Vakhilas' were also proved and marked as Exhibits-2-2(Ga). The learned Advocate also submits that the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Naogaon without rebutting the findings of the trial court adverting evidence on records, reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court illegally and in passing the impugned judgment and decree there has been misreading and non reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned counsel argued that the property-in-dispute had been correctly recorded in the name of plaintiff-petitioner in the field `bujarati khatian No.632 during the preparation of R.S. record of right and subsequently, the suit land have been wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No.2 and against that wrong record the plaintiff filed an Objection Case being No.195 of 1972 before the concerned settlement officer and the settlement officer on hearing both the parties allowed the objection Case No.195 of 1972 on 22.01.1972 A.D. vide Exhibit-5 and accordingly the government after acceptance of rents granted rent receipt in favour of the plaintiff vide Exihibit-6 and the learned appellate court was totally misconceived in appreciating the documentary evidences adduced from the plaintiffs side, which has been marked as Exhibits-1-8. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the government admitting the plaintiffs tenancy right to the suit property recognizing the plaintiff a tenant under government, granted rent receipt after accepting rents and the learned trial court after proper evaluation of the evidence on records conclusively held that the plaintiff has successfully discharged his onus of proof, but the defendants have hopelessly failed to disprove the case of the plaintiff and there is no evidence excepting the attested photocopy of the R.S. khatian No.1 marked as Exhibit-'Ka' from the side of the government to justify their case that the property has been vested to the government and the R.S. record of right has been rightly prepared, but the learned appellate court during disposal of the appeal without proper sifting of evidence in its true perspective and without proper appreciation of law, arbitrarily decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the appellant and passed the impugned judgment and decree, which is liable to be set aside. 

 10. In order to appreciate the argument advanced from the sides of the learned counsels for the respective parties, on perusal of the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.08.2011 and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in Other Class Suit No.66 of 1998, the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties and all other relevant papers including the case records it transpires that, admittedly the disputed property described in schedule `ka' of the plaint originally belonged to `Koibara Estate' and it is the pleading's case of the plaintiff that the Zamindar of the said estate from the C.S. plot No.733 settled 0.18 acres of land out of 2.43 acres of land in favour of one Krishna Mohon Fowjdar and in respect of the remaining land of schedule 'Ka', the Ex-Zamindar settled that land in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner on 27th Magh of 1351 B.S. The Zamindari papers have been produced from the side of the plaintiff, and these documents support the plaintiff's pleadings case and these papers after its formal proof under the Evidence Act, have been marked as Exhibit-1-2(Ka) and 2 (Ga) respectively. From the said Zamindari papers, it transpires that the Zamindar after accepting rent from the plaintiff granted rent receipts of their `Koibara Estate'. I also find from the documentary evidences adduced from the side of the plaintiff that the R.S. attested khatian No.107/5 was prepared in the name of plaintiff marked as Exhibit-3 and the papers relating to Objection Case No.195/1972 (Exhibit-5), the relevant attested khatian No. 632 and 107/5 in the name of the plaintiff-petitioner and the government rent received including the information slip relating to the positive contention of the plaintiff, go to show that the right to the plaintiff-petitioner in respect of the suit property has been accepted by the government-opposite party and all the official papers definitely have a presumptive value under the ambit of section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872. Besides this, it is also apparent from the rent receipt granted in favour of the plaintiff by the government that the government after accepting the rents from the plaintiff in respect of the suit property is now stopped from challenging the plaintiff's tenancy and it appears that, all these papers were properly evaluated by the trial court at the time of disposal of the Other Class Suit No.66 of 1998. 

 12. P.W.1 the plaintiff Kanai Lal in his testimony testified that he is the plaintiff to the suit and at a stage of his testimony he has categorically testified that, initially the draft S.A. khatian was prepared in his name and the S.A. attested khatian No.107/5 was prepared in the name of him and the field 'bujarat' khatian No.632 was also prepared in his name and subsequently while he came to know that the khatian has been finally published in the name of the defendant No.2, he filed an Objection Case being No.195/1972 which was allowed on contest and there has been an order from the office of the settlement officer that a khatian will be opened in his name (the plaintiff). The plaintiff in his deposition categorically testified that the legal heirs of Krishna Mohon Fowjdar after the death of Krishna Mohon transferred the land measuring 18 decimals in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner vide a registered sub-kabala deed dated 08.04.1997, which has been marked as Exhibit-8. During cross-examination from the side of the defendants, P.W.1 replied in a question that the property-in-dispute is never used by the people of the locality as `Shyrat Mohol, rather; the suit property is being used by him since his settlement. With regard to the boundaries of the suit land, P.W.1 Kanai Lal categorically testified about the boundary men, who are in possession in their lands, besides the suit land. 

 16. Vis-à-vis; the one and only witness of the defendant, D.W.1 Md. Abdul Mazid in his testimony testified that he is an Assistant Tahshildar of Hajinagar Union Land Office. He has brought the R.S. record book, wherefrom it appears that the suit property has been entried in khash khatian No.1. He has submitted the attested R.S. khatian which has been marked as Exhibit-'Ka'. During cross-examination D.W.1 in a reply to a question from the side of the plaintiff, testified that he has brought no paper showing that the suit land was ever possessed by the government through lease. D.W. 1, the concerned official witness of the government-opposite party in his testimony frankly admitted that the government rent receipt which has been produced from the side of the plaintiff, was issued by the government.

lawyer:
Md Khalilur Rahman with Junaed Hossen Khan with Md Rashidul Karim Advocates—For the Petitioners. 

Manzill Murshed, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 1. 

AKM Farhan, Advocate—For the Respondent.
parties:
Jahangir Alam (Md) and others ---------- Petitioners
Vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Gobinda Chandra Tagore J : On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why constituting a 7 (seven) member committee comprising of respondent Nos.2 to 8 under Memo No. 31.036.033.00. 00.221.2010-409(7) dated 27-7-2011 (Annexure-D) issued under the signature of respondent No.9 for investigating the finally published Dhaka City Survey Record-of-Rights in respect of 191 mouzas to ascertain the genuinity of such publication and to uphold/cancel the same and the report of the said committee dated 22-5-2012 (Annexure-E) and also the office order under Memo No. মপ/08/2011/83 dated 26-1-2012 issued by respondent No.10 (Annexure-F) forming two committees to investigate the alleged irregularities of the officials engaged in preparing and finally publishing the said Record-of-Rights, and thereby taking departmental actions against the petitioner and/or to initiate criminal cases under the Anti Corruption Law shall not be declared to have been done/issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondents shall not be directed to interfere with the quasi-judicial functions of the field level officers engaged in preparing and finally publishing the Record-of-Rights under the provisions of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and Tenancy Rules, 1955 in any manner, whatsoever other than under the provisions of the aforesaid Act and Rules and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, shall not be passed. 

 The petitioner No.1 is the President of Assistant Settlement Officer Welfare Association and the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are Secretary and Vice-President of the same Association of Dhaka unit. All of them are serving under the office of the Directorate of Land Records and Surveys as Non-Cadre Servants of the Government and were engaged in the preparation and publication of the recent Dhaka City Survey Khatians following the Dhaka City Survey, which were finally prepared and published in the Gazette Notification on different dates. The Directorate of Land Records and Surveys is empowered to prepare and publish the record-of-rights as per order issued by the Government from time to time by issuing Gazette Notification under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The employees and officers engaged in preparation and publication of the record-of-rights of that office are divided into two categories- Non-Cadre Service Holders starting from Chainman to Assistant Settlement Officer i.e. Chainman, Badar Amin, Sarder Amin, Halka Officer/Sub-Assistant Settlement Officer and Assistant Settlement Officer/Circle Officer and the other group belongs to the Cadre Service, who are deputed to the Directorate. The preparation and publication of the record-of-rights are quasi-judicial functions under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the Tenancy Rules, 1955, Survey and Settlement Manual, 1935, the Survey Act, 1875 and Technical Rules, 1957. The Rules 26-31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 are the main rules for preparing record-of-rights. Like judicial protection Act, 1850, section 77(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the rule 39 of the Tenancy Rule, 1955 and also the circular No. ভূঃমঃ/শাঃ-২(অডিট আপত্তি)-৭/২০০৬-৩৯০/১(৯০)dated 2-6-2008 issued by the Ministry of Land have given a safeguard to the persons involved in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights. The record-of-rights of Dhaka City Survey of 191 mouzas prepared under the Dhaka City Survey have already been completed and published in the Bangladesh Gazette as per rule 34 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 as well as, as per section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, except some of the khatians of each mouzas against which Writ Petitions or Civil proceedings are pending. When the dispute on finally publishing the record-of-rights were being adjudicated by the Land Survey Tribunals, the Ministry of Land suddenly issued the impugned office order bearing No. 31.036.033.00.00.221. 2010-409 dated 27-7-2011 forming an enquiry committee consisting of the respondent Nos.2-8 for giving an opinion either for affirming or cancelling the finally prepared and published City Survey Khatians of 191 Mouzas under the Dhaka City Survey after 5 years of publication of the same in the Gazette Notification. The said enquiry committee submitted the impugned report dated 22-5-2012 as contained in Annexure-E. In the said report, it was, amongst other, opined that approximately 2815.00 acres of the land of the Government were not recorded in the name of the Government while, most of those properties earlier belonged to the Court of Wards and subsequently, in the name of the private persons by operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. On receiving the said report dated 22-5-2012, the respondent No. 10, DGDLRS issued the impugned Memo No. মপ/০৮/২০১১/৮৩ dated 26-1-2012 forming two committees-one consisting of respondent Nos.11-15 and the other consisting of respondent Nos.16-19 to enquire into the matter in order to find out the irregularities in not recording the Government land and also to take action against the persons involved in such preparation and publication of the record-of-rights by starting departmental proceeding as well as by filing anti-corruption case against them. The petitioners being aggrieved by the said impugned orders and enquiry report contained in Annexures D, E and F filed the instant Writ Petition and obtained the Rule and the orders of stay and restraint. 

 5. The respondent No.1, the Ministry of Land contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition by denying the material allegations made in the Writ Petition and contending, inter alia, that the respondents, including the respondent Nos.11, 16 and 17 are not only responsible for management and administration of the Directorate or they are not only the supervising officer but they are also engaged in preparing and publishing record-of-rights. Therefore, the allegation made by the petitioners that the respondents are interfering with the so-called quasi-judicial function is not true. The superior officers starting from the post of Charge Officer of the DGLRS are legally authorized to supervise the official activities of the sub-ordinates of the Directorate. They also exercise their revenue powers for preparing and publishing of the record-of-rights in accordance with law as well as the instructions of the Government passed from time to time. Section 149(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 authorizes the Board of Land Administration to pass any order for correction of any entry in a record-of-rights maintained under Part-V of the Act or in a settlement-roll prepared and finally published under Part-V thereof. If there is any bonafide mistake, the superior officer of the Directorate may interfere with the functions and activities of the petitioners and others as per the provision of section 149(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950; rules 27, 28, 31, 36, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 42A 42B, and 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, the Technical Rules, and Chapter (iv) Rule 16, 19, 32 and Chapter (viii) rule-20 of Instructions of the Settlement Department, 1957. The position of a DGLRS is clearly manifested in rule 12 of Survey and Settlement Manual, 1935. The Government can issue circulars, memorandums and other instructions as per rules of Business and Allocation of Business and make rules under section 152 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Therefore, issuing circulars etc. by the Government or the Directorate for making it responsible and accountable is within the legal authority of the Government and the Directorate. Section 77(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 provides safeguard to the petitioners and others only if the acts are done in good faith. The circular dated 2-6-2008 was issued as a directive for the audit team to follow the same during auditing the field level offices. Rule 39 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 authorizes the Revenue Officer with the additional designation, Settlement Officer or Assistant Settlement Officer to exercise power like a Civil Court. The Rules do not give any immunity to the officials from accountability for their activities. The Revenue Officers and others engaged in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights cannot escape the responsibility and liability in securing the public interest in preparing the records-of-the public property. The respondents have every authority to look into whether the petitioners and others had any negligence or committed any deviation from the assigned tasks in preparing the records-of-land properly. Every judicial or quasi-judicial officer has a right to pass an order but it must be guided by the existing laws. The respondent Nos.11, 16 and 17 are empowered to exercise revenue powers and accordingly, they can look into the activities of their subordinate officers. The authority can hold any enquiry or form any committee to look into the allegations of any mischief or gross irregularities and negligence or intentionally done wrong activities committed by any of subordinate revenue officers at any stage of the survey. There are allegations published in different dailies that some revenue officers have recorded the land belonged to different public agencies in the name of some unscrupulous private persons although the previous record i.e. RS Record was in the name of public agencies and thus, helped misappropriation of the public lands by the land grabbers. The respondents are constitutionally bound to look into the serious allegations in public interest in order to take appropriate measures for recovery of the public property and also to take punitive measures against the persons found responsible for the misdeeds and causing losses to the state and public in general. There being serious allegation of irregularities against the finally published record-of-rights of 191 mouzas of City Survey, the respondents formed committee to scrutinize/investigate into the legal aspects as to whether there was any scope for cancellation of the records to redress the public sufferings and accordingly, the enquiry committee was formed by the Memo dated 27-7-2011. Moreover, no penal decision was taken against the petitioners. Accordingly, they cannot be aggrieved thereby and come before this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution for that purpose. No law or any rule gives any immunity to any officials involved in doing irregularities in the name of quasi-judicial functions or any public-office-functions. The petitioners having done gross irregularities in publishing the record-of-rights cannot claim the safeguards under the law and circular as has been claimed by them. The impugned orders were very much within the purview of law. The impugned report contains the facts based on the case studies. The petitioners could have sought relief through normal official procedure and there was nothing to worry about the said impugned order and reports unless he or she is found to have done anything wrong in malafide intention. Hence, the Writ Petition is not maintainable. 

 6. Having placed the Writ Petition, Mr Md Khalilur Rahman along with Mr Junaed Hossen Khan and Mr Md Rashidul Karim, learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that since the record-of-rights prepared finally has already been published in the official Gazette, the Government including the respondents have no legal authority under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act to cancel the same and the aggrieved persons including any Government agencies can take recourse to law before the Land Survey Tribunal for correcting the errors, if any, in preparing the said record-of-rights and, as such, the impugned orders as contained in Annexures D and E and the report prepared in pursuance thereof as contained in Annexure-E are liable to be declared to have been passed or prepared without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. 

 13. The petitioners and others were involved in preparing and publishing the Dhaka City record-of-rights following the Dhaka City Survey. The record-of-rights have already been finalized and published in the official Gazette. As per the case of the respondents, there were serious allegations of irregularities and illegalities in conducting survey and preparing and publishing the record-of-rights. Even 2815.0569 acres of land appertaining to 191 mouza of Dhaka have been wrongly and illegally recorded in the name of private persons through the petitioners and others, who were involved in conducting the survey and preparing and publishing the record-of-rights. In order to ascertain the liability of the persons involved in such illegalities or irregularities, the respondent No.1, Ministry of Land issued the impugned office order dated 27-7-2011 as contained in Annexure-D forming an Enquiry Committee for a recommendation whether the record-of-rights of the said 191 mouzas should be maintained or cancelled. The Enquiry Committee upon enquiry submitted a report dated 22-5-2012 and the said report was forwarded to the Secretary, Ministry of Land by the impugned Memo dated 22-5-2012. But it appears from the said report dated 22-5-2012 that it was an incomplete report and thereby the liability of the persons involved in preparing such illegal and erroneous record-of-rights was not ascertained. Accordingly, the Directorate of Land Record and Survey by the impugned office order dated 26-1-2012 formed two committees underlining the terms of reference of the committee as under: 

 15. It appears from the Writ Petition that the petitioners filed the Writ Petition with an apprehension only that upon such enquiry, departmental and punitive measures may be taken against them. But it appears from the said office order dated 26-1-2012, Annexure-F that it was intended not to take punitive measures against all the persons, who were involved in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights but only against the persons who are liable for committing any irregularity and illegality. Thus, it appears from the said impugned orders as contained in Annexures D, E and F that the Ministry of Land or the Directorate of Land Record and Survey has yet not completed the enquiry fixing the liability of the persons responsible for any illegality. However, once the record-of-rights, whether it was prepared wrongly or rightly has already been published in the official Gazette, the respondents have no legal authority under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 to cancel the same by any administrative order. The same can only be cancelled or altered or corrected by the competent Court of civil jurisdiction. 

 17. In such facts and circumstances, it appears that the Writ Petition is pre-mature while, the respondents have no legal authority to cancel the record-of-rights published finally.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 422 of 2010
lawyer:
Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner
Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Principal and Secretary, Nawabgonj Government College, Nawabgonj ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Mahabuba Khatun (Dolly) and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. This Civil Petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.07.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 358 of 2002 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 05.02.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Nawabgonj in Other Class Suit No. 57 of 1987 dismissing the suit. The plaintiff-respondent herein filed the above mentioned Other Class Suit No. 57 of 1987 for declaration of title and partition. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that 4.02 acres of land as described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint originally belonged to 3 brothers, namely, Ashutosh Chatyapadhya, Sharat Chandra Chatyapadhya and Monimdra Chatyapadhya in equal share and the C.S. Khatian was accordingly prepared in their names. That after partition of Pakistan and India Sharat Chandra Migrated to India and arranged an exchange of his share i.e. .95 acre out of schedule 'Ka' land with Indian land of one Ishahaque Mia-the father of the plaintiffs. That for effecting the exchange Sharat Chandra executed a power of attorney in favour of one Harun-ar-Rashid. Harun-ar-Rashid having obtained necessary permission from the then District Collector, Rajshahi, executed and registered a deed of exchange dated 13.10.1952 in favour of Ishahaque Mia. Thus Ishahaque Mia having acquired title and possession in the suit land had been in possession and enjoyment of the same for long 20 years within the knowledge of all including the defendants, Nawabgonj Government College and others. That Ishahaque Mia while in possession of the suit land executed a power of attorney in favour of Harun-ar-Rashid who being so empowered executed and registered two hiba-bil-ewaj deeds dated 09.10.1974 transferring the said .94 acre of land of Ishahaque Mia in favour of his daughters, the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 4. Thus the plaintiffs acquired the suit land and since acquisition they have been in possession of the same by paying rent to the government to the knowledge of all including the defendants. That the defendant college subsequently purchased 2/3rd share of 'Ka' schedule land from Ashutosh and Monindra and has been in ejamali possession of that land with Ishahaque Mia and thereafter with the plaintiffs. That the 'Ka' schedule land has never been partitioned by metes and bounds among these co-sharers. That only in the month of October, 1985 when an employee of the plaintiffs went to pay rent in the local Tahsil Office the Tahsildar disclosed that the land was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 College in R.S. Khatian and was finally published. That this R.S. record of the land in the name of the college in 16 annas share is wrong and collusive. That on the basis of this wrong recording the defendant college claimed title in the entire 'Ka' schedule land and thus the title of the plaintiffs in the suit has been clouded and hence the suit. 

 2. The defendant college and the government contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. These defendants admit the title of 3 C.S. recorded tenants and subsequently also of Ishahaque Mia in the 'Ka' schedule land. But their case is that the defendant college being established in the then newly created Nawabgonj Sub-Division purchased 95 1/2 decimals of land of 'Ka' schedule from Ashutosh Chattapadhya by a registered sale deed dated 23.02.1957 and also purchased the other 95 1/2 decimals of land from Monindra Chatyapadhya Chandra by registered sale deed dated 12.04.1957. That the share of Sharat Chandra was transferred to Ishahaque Mia by way of exchange and the said Ishahaque Mia transferred his 95 1/2 decimals of land to the college by an oral gift in presence of many and the college authority accepted it with gratitude. These defendants stated also that out of 4.02 acres of land described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint 2.86 acres of land only finally stood as rest 1.16 acres fell into road and ditches. That the college authority thus, is in possession of 2.86 acres of land of the 'Ka' schedule to the knowledge of all including the plaintiffs. This land has been duly recorded in the name of the college in R.S. khatian. The college authority has erected wall on the west and northern side of the R.S. plot few years ago. The college authority is in possession of the suit land for more than 12 years and as such they have acquired title by adverse possession also. That the plaintiffs have filed this suit on false claim suppressing the real facts. 

 4. On appeal the High Court Division set aside the findings and decision of the trial court and decreed the suit making observations and findings to the effect that the plaintiffs being daughters of the admitted co-sharers have succeeded in proving their title to the extent of 1/3rd share in the land described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint and that the defendants could not prove their claim that the father, of the plaintiffs transferred his 1/3rd share in the 'Ka' schedule land in favour of the defendant college by oral gift and that the defendant college could not prove also its claim that the college has acquired title in this land by adverse possession also and that the recording of the 'Ka' schedule land in the name of the defendant college in 16 annas in R.S. Khatian has been wrong.
